raw_title: ‘Dangerous’ but also ‘brilliant’
title: Dangerous' but also 'brilliant
raw_summary: New Haas driver Rafa Camara received a reprimand on his Formula 1 debut for what was deemed “clearly dangerous” impeding of Charles Leclerc in Brazilian Grand Prix practice. Camara weaved and moved into the racing line as he prepared to start a push lap in FP2 at Interlagos just as Leclerc was coming by to complete a lap of his own.
summary: New Haas driver Rafa Camara received a reprimand on his Formula 1 debut for what was deemed “clearly dangerous” impeding of Charles Leclerc in Brazilian Grand Prix practice. Camara weaved and moved into the racing line as he prepared to start a push lap in FP2 at Interlagos just as Leclerc was coming by to complete a lap of his own.
article_paragraphs: New Haas driver Rafa Camara received a reprimand on his Formula 1 debut for what was deemed “clearly dangerous” impeding of Charles Leclerc in Brazilian Grand Prix practice.
Camara weaved and moved into the racing line as he prepared to start a push lap in FP2 at Interlagos just as Leclerc was coming by to complete a lap of his own.

Though he was warned several times that Leclerc was approaching, Camara ended up squeezing the Ferrari towards the run-off at high speed “with a significant amount of the car off the track”, said the stewards, who upgraded the typical practice penalty for impeding from a warning to a formal reprimand.
“The situation that was created was clearly dangerous and [Camara] should have taken more care to avoid impeding [Leclerc]."
Camara’s incident with Leclerc was a blot on an otherwise solid and steadily improving first day in the car.

He finished 0.86s slower than Ollie Bearman in FP1, and trimmed the gap to 0.57s in FP2, with the biggest part of his time lost in the middle sector - although he had been even closer on the initial hard-tyre push laps before switching to softs.
There was a recurring problem under braking into Turn 1, where Camara had huge run-ending lock-ups in both FP1 and FP2, although several drivers had trouble here.
And he was still trying to smoothen his throttle usage exiting Turns 2 and 12 by the end of Friday as well.

If there's anything that the Kia Telluride has always been good at, it's making a first impression. In fact, that's especially true compared to most of the rest of the competition in the segment. Kia even mixes in a little Range Rover flair, which is a weird thing to say if you knew this brand well about 20 years ago.

Spend a week with it, like we just did, and the details inside the cabin are equally impressive. It's spacious, the controls make sense, and the equipment list includes a massaging front driver's seat. Kia has unquestionably put together a compelling package here on the spec sheet. Our 2027 Kia Telluride X-Pro SX Prestige (boy, is that a handful of a name) sits at the top of the lineup, starting at $58,335 including the $1,545 destination charge. That's serious money for a family SUV, but after living with this one for a week, it's also a price we can understand.

Kia did an excellent job with the exterior. The Telluride has presence from pretty much every angle, and the side profile is particularly strong. It retains enough of its established character to feel familiar while moving the design forward considerably. Let's start with the area over the tires. Look closely at the creases over the fenders . Those lines are unusually tight, giving the sheet metal definition that softer surfacing would have lost. Now, check out the hood. It gets similarly crisp detailing, and together those elements make the whole SUV look substantial and deliberate.

There's a temptation in vehicle design to round off the edges until it becomes broadly agreeable. Kia has committed to the shape, and the result with the Telluride is significant. It will unquestionably stand out in a sea of other three-row family haulers. We can't say that for many of the others in the game, especially at this price point.

The Range Rover resemblance comes through in the proportions and overall presence. It still has its own identity, particularly when you start following the individual body lines. To our eyes, it's an excellent evolution, and one that has a good chance of aging well. It's also worth noting that the X-Pro's 18-inch wheels and all-terrain tires suit the design. They give it an appropriately purposeful stance without needing enormous wheels to fill out the look.

The cabin is ultimately where this SUV begins to really impress. Sure, it looks good on the outside but the reality is that plenty of vehicles that look great from outside the cabin wither inside. What's good about it you ask? Mostly the cohesive, consistent, and logical design choices. Let's start out with the switchgear.

Climate adjustments get physical controls. Temperature, fan speed, and airflow changes are readily accessible, and Kia provides physical shortcuts for frequently used infotainment functions too. The center stack gives you plenty to operate directly, which makes everyday adjustments straightforward. The volume control sits in the middle of the stack, where either front occupant can reach it.

article_paragraphs: Apollo has spent the last several years carving out a spot for itself toward the more premium end of the electric scooter market. Now the company is trying something different: going after the mass market with its least expensive model yet.

The new Apollo Dash carries a $699 MSRP, but is launching at $599 as part of the company’s Black Friday sale running through November 30. More importantly, Apollo says the Dash isn’t intended to simply be a stripped-down budget scooter, but rather a way to bring much of its existing technology down to a lower price point.

The scooter uses a 48V electrical system powering a 600W nominal, 1,200W peak-rated Bosch motor, with a top speed of 20 mph (32 km/h). Its 480Wh battery is rated for up to 25 miles (40 km) of range in Eco mode.

Apollo also claims the 48V architecture avoids limiting motor power to anemic levels as the battery drains, meaning riders shouldn’t experience the same increasingly sluggish performance toward the bottom of the battery that can occur on some lower-cost scooters.

At 43 lb (19.5 kg), the Dash is reasonably portable, though getting the weight and price down comes with an important compromise: there’s no suspension. Apollo also caps rider weight at 220 lb (100 kg), and points heavier riders or those regularly tackling rough roads and hills toward the more expensive Apollo Go instead.

Despite the lower price, there’s still a surprisingly long feature list. The Dash gets IP66 water resistance, self-healing tubeless tires, regenerative braking, built-in turn signals, Apollo’s Beam stem light, NFC unlocking, Apple Find My integration, and connectivity with the Apollo smartphone app.

Apollo says it put the frame through 10,000 km (6,200 miles) of durability validation before shipping production units. A beta test program also accumulated 1,002 miles over 144 rides without any reported punctures or maintenance issues. Beta riders averaged 19 miles (30 km) per ride while finishing with 29% battery remaining, according to Apollo.

Perhaps the bigger story here, though, is where Apollo is positioning the Dash. The company says 52% of its customers previously owned scooters from brands including Segway, NIU, and Xiaomi, but historically moving up to an Apollo often meant crossing the $1,000 mark.

raw_summary: You get them. I get them. We all get them. AI robocalls are a nightmare scourge on society that are driving everybody to the brink of their sanity. Usually, they're from some sort of money-lending organization. Still, one Massachusetts man says he keeps receiving pre-recorded phone calls from Cambridge Honda asking him whether he was interested in selling them his car. Now, he's seeking class-action status against the dealership, alleging that it violated the Telephone Consumer Protection Act. If you're open to an instant cash offer on your car, give me a call at (351) 300-0683. Thanks." Kamens added that he received subsequent texts from "Roger" inviting him to sell his vehicle — something he really has no interest in doing.

If you're open to an instant cash offer on your car, give me a call at (351) 300-0683. Thanks." Kamens added that he received subsequent texts from "Roger" inviting him to sell his vehicle — something he really has no interest in doing.

In an effort to get answers, Kamens called the number back. A voice at the other end answered, but when he started the conversation asking if the person was real or not, it said it was AI, according to AutoNews , which received the same automated response when it called the number.

Kamens says he filed the suit on behalf of everyone in the U.S. who has received a pre-recorded message from Cambridge Honda on their cell phones over the past four years. The complaint asserts that folks who got these calls were "temporarily deprived of legitimate use of their phone because the phone line was tied up, they were charged for the calls and their privacy was improperly invaded."
"Moreover, the call injured [Kamens] because it was frustrating, obnoxious, annoying and a nuisance and disturbed [his] solitude," it said.
While this is true, it's also funny to think about suing someone because they took away from your screen time. I mean, I would, but you get what I'm saying.

The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts, asked for certification of the class, damages and an order prohibiting Cambridge Honda from "making calls, except for emergency purposes, to any cellular telephone numbers using an artificial or prerecorded voice in the future." The Honda dealer, for its part, has remained quiet. A lawyer representing the store said she wasn't authorized to discuss the case.
It's not clear how many times Kamens was contacted by the dealer or how many people in total were impacted, but if they're going for a class action, my gut tells me it's not "a few."

For example, the red and green needles on the pressure gauges are inspired by Porsche colors. The dials feature "RS" and "2.7" badges. The side of the machine gets its own limited edition "One of 911" plaque.

Three color schemes are available. Buyers in America can select from white and green or tangerine and black. Production for each paint color is limited to just 911 examples. Germany also has a region-specific version painted in white and blue, just like the 911 Carrera RS 2.7 . There are only 150 units of it to go around. Does all of that explain why it's evidently worth $7,911 before tax? Probably not, but let's at least get into the details of what each machine offers in terms of tech specs.

These espresso makers are all modeled on La Marzocco's Linea Micra machine. They get a convertible portafilter that can use a single spout, double spout, or a bottomless configuration. Users can leverage an app to adjust temperatures and schedule brew times. The water tank holds two liters, and there's even some LED lighting to add a little drama. The ducktail spoiler motif is part of the cup holder on top — a simple, subtle nod.

The brands also collaborated on a grinder modeled after La Marzocco's Pico. It's available in the same colors and costs $2,125 before tax. The machine allows three memory settings, stepless grind adjustment, and manual grinding. A magnetically adjustable portafilter and self-closing hopper add some convenience that can help this machine stand out a little. Of course, the RS lettering and collaboration logos all do that to their own degree. Combined, the set costs $10,036 before tax and shipping. Boy, do I feel less terrible about a $20 Starbucks order.

For those of you with well over $10,000 burning a hole in your pocket, I have good news. There's plenty more Porsche coffee stuff to buy. That includes a coffee aroma tin for just $135. There are also barista napkins — I am not joking — for the nice price of $69. Porsche is also selling miniature versions of the 911 Carrera RS 2.7 that match the coffee makers' paint schemes.

In case that wasn't enough, the company also sells several versions of espresso cups. The ones that match these machines sell as a two-pack with saucers for $105. Those willing to go for most of the other designs can get just an espresso cup for around $35. The last set of espresso machines sold out in eight hours. I wouldn't be shocked if these do the same.

title: The Yangwang U9 Xtreme Just Set Two Guinness World Speed Records
raw_summary: The fastest production car in the world. No, not necessarily an attribute that would be useful in your real life, unless your driveway is a section of unrestricted autobahn, but as an achievement, it's something automakers love to boast about. Porsche. Ferrari. Bugatti. And now Yangwang. The luxury division of Chinese giant BYD (as Lexus is to Toyota), Yangwang's appropriately named U9 Xtreme hypercar just hit 312 mph on a public road in Abu Dhabi. This feat nets it two Guinness World Records at once: the single-direction highest speed for both a production car and for a production electric car.

article_paragraphs: The fastest production car in the world. No, not necessarily an attribute that would be useful in your real life, unless your driveway is a section of unrestricted autobahn, but as an achievement, it's something automakers love to boast about. Porsche. Ferrari. Bugatti. And now Yangwang.

The luxury division of Chinese giant BYD (as Lexus is to Toyota), Yangwang's appropriately named U9 Xtreme hypercar just hit 312 mph on a public road in Abu Dhabi. This feat nets it two Guinness World Records at once: the single-direction highest speed for both a production car and for a production electric car.

At this point, perhaps the electric production speed record doesn't need its own subdivision, especially since the U9 was chiefly breaking its own previous record of 308 mph, set last year. The U9 Xtreme, or U9X, has four electric motors, one at each wheel, for a grand total of over 3000 hp. That's three Veyrons concentrated into a single car.

The battery architecture is also distinct from the standard U9, with a 1200-volt architecture and the ability to both send and receive huge amounts of power with greatly improved thermal efficiency. Even when nearly depleted, at 20 percent charge, it can still pump out 1800 kilowatts of power (2414 hp), or soak up 700 kilowatts through regenerative braking.

A motor at each corner means almost limitless fine-tuning for torque-vectoring control, meting out all that power with minimal wheelslip. The U9X also features electric dampers that clamp down on squat and dive under hard acceleration and braking, and active aerodynamic elements to maintain stability at speed. A tip of the hat also goes to Indonesia's Giti Tires, who developed the rubber capable of putting up with these tremendous speeds and forces.

Yangwang only plans to build thirty of these U9X models, and it's not like you can just slap on a license plate and bully 911 Turbos on the Autobahn. The 4.35-mile stretch of public road used for the record attempt was closed at the time, and also fastidiously cleaned of debris, including going back over the surface looking for any wires left by the street sweepers.

However, as a demonstration of just how advanced BYD's battery chemistry can be, this new speed record represents all kinds of bragging rights. Speed records come and go. For now, nothing can touch the Yangwang U9 Xtreme.

One thing Chevy wasn't able to retain from previous iterations of the Corvette was a manual transmission. article_paragraphs: Chevrolet nailed the supercar brief with the C8 Corvette, building a car that can rival the best from Europe at a much more affordable price point. Peitz Performance is behind the manual C8 . It has teamed up with Tremec to bring the transmission manufacturer's new six-speed manual transaxle into the C8 Corvette , creating a car that 'Vette enthusiasts have been clamoring for. Tremec's new transaxle was unveiled at last year's SEMA Show and can support up to 1,000 pound-feet of torque and accommodate the screaming 8,600 rpm redline of the fiery Z06.

Fitting a six-speed manual into the C8 Corvette isn't easy. Peitz replaces the car's standard eight-speed dual-clutch transmission in favor of Tremec's TR9060 and adds a concentric slave cylinder, a modified clutch pedal from a Cadillac CT4-V Blackwing, and a new flywheel and clutch. The key to ensuring the six-speed works with the C8 is the MoTeC M182 plug-and-play ECU controller and the MoTeC M150 transmission control unit.

Peitz says the new TCU allows for precise blips while downshifting and upshift ignition cuts, in addition to controlling important data like the clutch pedal position, gear position, and transmission fluid temperature. The M182 control module allows for fine-tuning of the C8's powertrain, allowing the tuner to add things like rolling anti-lag, adjustable traction control, and the fitment of nitrous and methanol systems.

In July, Californian firm Rezvani unveiled its own gated manual for the C8 Corvette , built in partnership with Italy's Studio Carrozzi. The catch of this system is that it isn't a true manual like Tremec's and simply serves as an add-on to the existing dual-clutch transmission. In fact, it doesn't even include a clutch pedal, and the driver doesn't need to lift off the gas to change gears. What Peitz is offering is a full, traditional manual swap for the Corvette, giving the world a 'Vette that not even Chevrolet itself has been willing to build.

The only not-so-exciting thing about the Peitz's manual C8 swap is the cost. The company is charging $74,528 for its three-pedal transformation, which gets you all the hardware and software for the swap but you still need to provide the donor car. To put this price tag into perspective, you can buy a brand-new 2027 Corvette Stingray from as little as $73,795 including delivery.

raw_title: You Can Now Rent A Tesla With FSD On Turo
title: You Can Now Rent A Tesla With FSD On Turo
raw_summary: If you've ever wondered what it's like to ride in a Tesla with the Full Self-Driving (Supervised) system enabled, now could be your chance. Last month, Turo announced that users can now search for and book Teslas that are equipped with the carmaker's latest advanced driver-assistance system. As with Tesla owners, Turo users experimenting with FSD will need to stay vigilant, or else they could end up on the news for all the wrong reasons . Despite what its name suggests, Tesla's FSD system is only a Level 2 system. This means it is not technically a hands-off, eyes-off, or mind-off system, where the driver can completely relax while behind the wheel. As a result, Turo is encouraging users to read Tesla's Full Self-Driving (Supervised) safety documentation before booking a ride. That's smart on Turo's part, but we can't help but think very few users will bother, and they'll probably end up booking Teslas they think are fully autonomous, only to find out they're not. That sounds like a recipe for disaster.

As part of the Turo app update, users can now search specifically for Tesla vehicles that are equipped with FSD . The app also displays a message reading 'Your Tesla will be able to drive itself almost anywhere with minimal driver intervention.' Although that may be true, such a bold proclamation could lead some passengers to let their guard down from the driver's seat, which, again, isn't a wise idea with FSD.

There are already thousands of FSD-enabled Teslas available on Turo . Tesla owners who already have their vehicle listed on Turo but don't have FSD can get a free one-month subscription to try it. Vehicles must have the latest Tesla AI4 hardware, and the owner must have completed at least one trip as a Turo host. Fortunately for users, FSD cannot be listed as a paid extra, though there's nothing stopping hosts from increasing rental fees if their car has FSD.

Hosts are also being encouraged to warn guests that the Full Self-Driving (Supervised) system requires their full attention and that they remain in charge of the vehicle. In addition, guests should be warned that the system may suddenly stop operating if the cameras are obstructed.

Drivers of compatible non-Tesla EVs can start a session through the Tesla app. If you drive a Tesla, the charging station shows up in the car’s navigation and Trip Planner. Other EVgo fast chargers with NACS plugs have been showing up in Tesla navigation since early September if you turn on third-party charging.
“By serving both Tesla and non-Tesla NACS drivers, we’re doubling EVgo’s addressable market and continuing to meet EV drivers where they are and where they want to charge,” said Badar Khan, EVgo CEO.
EVgo owns the Superchargers and self-brands them, and Tesla runs and maintains them. The first sites will be at Regency Centers shopping plazas with grocery stores.

EVgo is also adding NACS plugs to its regular fast-charging network, a rollout it started in 2025. The company aims to have 500 of those stalls across the US by the end of 2026, with Supercharger stalls counted separately. article_paragraphs: There's little question that automated license plate reader (ALPR) technology, and most notably Flock Safety , has had a long year under the microscope. A new case from Florida helps to explain some of that scrutiny on more than a single level. According to Pinellas County Sheriff Bob Gualtieri , one of his now-former deputies misused the ALPR system over 100 times to track his estranged wife, her new boyfriend, and other family members. If that wasn't bad enough, the sheriff's response to criticism of Flock is now drawing its own critiques.

The now-former deputy is Ronald Scott, 35, who resigned from the department a day before his arrest on November 5. Up until that point, he'd worked in the department for 10½ years. Police charged him with three counts of accessing a computer/electronic device without authority and one count of official misconduct. Those are serious charges, and they bring to light one of the biggest issues with ALPR technology.

Authorities say they only caught Scott's behavior after an "enhanced system audit" identified his alleged improper access. They say the searches started this Valentine's Day and stopped June 19, meaning it took 8½ months once he started for the department to catch him, leaving Scott out there doing police work the whole time.

Critics call this out regularly. Audit logs and recommendations about data are only so good as the people who enforce them. There seems to be no mechanism for stopping an officer from misusing the system outside of the possibility that they might get caught. Scott allegedly used several false explanations as to why he was conducting these searches; police don't need a warrant to search these databases and, in some instances, don't even need as much as a case number. Still, that hasn't stopped Sheriff Gualtieri from defending the technology.

"As I've repeatedly said, this is a people problem, not an ALPR problem," he said. "The issue of people with access to confidential databases misusing those databases for personal reasons has existed forever ... we will monitor and take appropriate action when we find misuse." He said he's confident that this is the last "historical" misuse the department will uncover. That's quite the assertion, considering that Scott is the third Pinellas deputy arrested for this sort of misuse over the last few months.

Gualtieri does deserve credit for admitting one thing : "You can't fix stupid, and you can't keep people from doing dumb things." Whether the solution is letting people make mistakes at the risk of the public and personal privacy, or removing the government's ability to track people via ALPR devices, is the debate everyone will continue to have. This case certainly won't quiet that down.

This followed several secret and unofficial votes between the MotoGP riders, in which the majority had voted against holding a Qatar race due to fears of conflict escalation in the Middle East.
In the end, though, only the Yamaha riders - those representing the factory team and the satellite team Pramac - are absent from the Qatar GP without replacement.

Yamaha announced last Sunday that it "had not identified sufficient grounds to change its existing company-wide travel restrictions" to send its teams to Qatar, a decision that was met with "disappointment" and suggestion of "sporting consequences" from MotoGP.
The series emphasised it did not "receive any information that would warrant a change to the current plans for the event" after consultation with Qatar, the track and "independent safety advisors".
As for the riders present in Qatar, some have taken a more conciliatory stance over the handling of the event, but others have maintained a more confrontational tone.

Notably, seven-time series champion Marc Marquez said in the pre-event press conference: "I would like to be in another place. For that reason I arrive on the latest flight possible, and I will leave on the earliest flight possible."

In fact, the gap the lead Mercedes had over a mixed-up cast of would-be contenders at Interlagos reflected how 2026 has tended to play out overall.
Norris, Max Verstappen's Red Bull and George Russell's Mercedes were covered by just 0.020s, while Oscar Piastri was fifth in the second McLaren only half a tenth further back.

Verstappen was once again displeased with some engine behaviour in this session - and his confusion over Red Bull’s slightly vague update on how it was "adapting" to him prompted an amusing radio exchange where Verstappen suggested he should start talking to the clutch directly.
Less funny was the fact he ended the session early in the garage as a steering issue emerged that Red Bull could not quickly resolve.
In performance terms, the outlier at the moment is Ferrari, which seems to be struggling on balance but also (as usual) with straightline speed.

Lewis Hamilton led the team in sixth, nearly three tenths ahead of Charles Leclerc – who survived a high-speed near-miss when F1 debutant Rafa Camara’s Haas inadvertently squeezed him coming onto the start-finish straight.

raw_title: The 2027 Karma Gyesera Is a Stylish Curiosity
title: The 2027 Karma Gyesera Is a Stylish Curiosity
raw_summary: Henrik Fisker probably had no idea how fitting the name Karma would be when he launched the plug-in hybrid sedan in 2011 under his eponymous startup. In Hinduism, karma is intrinsically linked to reincarnation, the karma accumulated in one life affecting the conditions of the next life. Fisker’s venture wound up failing in 2014, but after Wanxiang Group, a Chinese automotive parts conglomerate, bought the assets, the car was reborn as the Karma Revero. The Revero has been built since 2016 and has undergone several updates, but the tiny California-based company has struggled to gain a foothold. Now Karma Automotive is seeking to reinvent itself, and it will start by giving the plug-in hybrid sedan yet another reincarnation. Marques McCammon—previously of DaimlerChrysler, Roush, Saleen, and engineering firm Ricardo—joined as president of the company in 2023, and the 2027 Gyesera is the first product launched under his guidance. While it retains similarities to the sedans that preceded it, a lightly updated powertrain and a fresh design language aim to set the brand up for a brighter future. Driving a pre-production version of the Gyesera in and around Las Vegas, we discovered a car that feels special and provides enticing powertrain flexibility but that is still bound by some of the same flaws as its predecessors.

Fisker’s venture wound up failing in 2014, but after Wanxiang Group, a Chinese automotive parts conglomerate, bought the assets, the car was reborn as the Karma Revero. The Revero has been built since 2016 and has undergone several updates, but the tiny California-based company has struggled to gain a foothold.

Now Karma Automotive is seeking to reinvent itself, and it will start by giving the plug-in hybrid sedan yet another reincarnation. Marques McCammon—previously of DaimlerChrysler, Roush, Saleen, and engineering firm Ricardo—joined as president of the company in 2023, and the 2027 Gyesera is the first product launched under his guidance. While it retains similarities to the sedans that preceded it, a lightly updated powertrain and a fresh design language aim to set the brand up for a brighter future. Driving a pre-production version of the Gyesera in and around Las Vegas, we discovered a car that feels special and provides enticing powertrain flexibility but that is still bound by some of the same flaws as its predecessors.

The Gyesera was initially revealed in 2024 as a fully electric vehicle , but Karma Automotive pivoted when it determined that the luxury market wasn’t moving toward EVs fast enough. Instead of the originally proposed 590-hp battery-electric setup, the Gyesera now launches with a fifth generation of the Karma’s plug-in hybrid powertrain. A turbocharged 1.5-liter three-cylinder engine—borrowed from the BMW i8 —lives under the hood, but it isn’t connected to the wheels. Instead, it acts as a generator to charge the 28-kWh battery, which then feeds electricity to a pair of motors on the rear axle.

The Gyesera produces 566 horsepower—30 hp more than the Revero—and 594 pound-feet of torque, an increase of 44. Karma says the Gyesera accelerates from zero to 60 mph in 3.7 seconds, down from 4.5 seconds in the Revero, and can hit a 150-mph top speed, up from the Revero’s 125-mph V-max. The nickel-manganese-cobalt battery is also capable of providing a claimed 80 miles of electric-only driving, with a total range on gasoline of 360 miles. The battery can support DC fast-charging via a CCS port at up to 50 kilowatts or AC charging at 6.6 kilowatts.

As you approach the Gyesera, it makes a strong first impression. There remains more than a whiff of the original Fisker Karma in its appearance, with the Gyesera using an evolution of the aluminum spaceframe chassis found in previous Karmas. Design-wise, this is no bad thing. The proportions look exotic, with a hood that seems to go on forever and a roofline that tapers over the muscular rear haunches. The curvaceous body is fashioned from a mix of aluminum and carbon fiber, the latter comprising the hood, rear decklid, fenders, rocker panels, and optionally, the roof.

While the shape is familiar, the design has been sharpened. Up front, a crisp line runs underneath piercing headlights, replacing the black grille trim that made the Revero look like an athlete wearing a mouthguard. The lower air intake is framed by a carbon-fiber trim piece, while a swooping indent, which Karma calls the Comet Line, arcs across the hood, giving the car a powerful look and serving as a hot air outlet for the engine bay. A strip of exposed, unpainted carbon fiber at the top of the hood is a reminder of the Gyesera’s high-end construction.

The forged aluminum wheels are the fruit of a partnership with HRE, with two different 21-inch designs available along with a 22-inch option. The smooth sides are broken up by a carbon-fiber trim piece carved into the front fender, and at the rear, slim taillights sit above a subtle diffuser. The Gyesera’s visual drama is even more apparent in person, and even amid the fancy cars in Vegas, the Gyesera turned heads on the Strip.

Inside, Karma revised the dashboard, ditching the Revero’s four circular air vents for rectangular vents hidden within a black trim piece that spans the dash. The 10.1-inch screen has been repositioned and is paired with a 12.3-inch digital gauge cluster. Some things remain unchanged from the Revero, such as the pyramid-like push-button gear selector and the steering wheel, which still has an echo of the original Fisker Karma’s design.

At the classic 4.3km Interlagos circuit, Antonelli set his quickest time just before the halfway mark of FP2 as drivers moved towards soft-tyre running, the Italian going faster than Lando Norris and Max Verstappen.

Despite fans intermittently reaching for their ponchos, light drops of rain never really persisted on what was predicted to be the clearest day of a rain-affected weekend. But the cooler, overcast conditions did affect the running in different ways, as Lewis Hamilton reported he "can't get the tyre temperatures up". Hamilton was one of several drivers to lock up the front-left wheel on approach to the heavily cambered Turn 1.

Antonelli, who became F1's youngest ever world champion last weekend in Mexico, suffered from heavy bottoming on the bumpy layout, but still managed to lead the early running on hard tyres with a 1m11.8 lap.

Following a quieter spell, the paddock collectively unwrapped Pirelli's soft tyre compound. Russell, who has a five-place grid penalty overhanging his weekend for taking a new engine, came to the fore with a 1m11.016s lap, before being demoted by Norris and Verstappen.

Russell's Mercedes partner Antonelli went quicker still, dipping below the 1m11 barrier with a 1m10.763s effort. That was a quarter of a second quicker than three drivers from three different teams, such is the convergence of performance towards the end of the 2026 season.

In the upgraded McLaren MCL40, which boasts a new front wing, Norris took second with a 1m11.016s lap, which was 0.006s ahead of third-placed Verstappen, who caused some hilarity with his radio complaints about his Red Bull's clutch.

Russell and Oscar Piastri all followed within a tenth of Norris to complete the top five. Ferrari , often strong out of the gates on Friday, had an unusually muted start in Brazil. After going quickest in the first sector, Hamilton settled for sixth with team-mate Charles Leclerc in seventh, Leclerc rueing being impeded on the straight by Haas debutant Rafael Camara.

The Cybertruck was promised as a full sized, five-seat electric pickup truck with ample storage room. Tesla delivered on the zero emission angle, of course, and the five seats, too. However, the automaker failed to deliver on pickup truckyness in any substantive way (see entire CleanTechnica archive here ).

title: This Modified Fiat Topolino Could Cost You More Than A New Honda Civic Hybrid
raw_summary: Fiat's all-electric Topolino microcar is small in stature but big on style and character, evoking a time when cars weren't unnecessarily big, heavy, or boring. It has now attracted the attention of Belgian firm Cavalier, which has unveiled a slew of customizations that boost its looks and performance. The only catch is price: a fully equipped Topolino from Cavalier costs as much as a brand-new Honda Civic Hybrid in the U.S. With that in mind, only the most enthusiastic Topolino owners will probably be interested. Cavalier's touches start with the paint. Customers can order their bespoke Topolino in one of ten available two-tone paint schemes, ranging from Ivory White with Sage Green to Deep Black and Deep Bordeaux Red, and our favorite of the bunch: Light Silver Grey with Warm Terracotta Orange. If you don't like the two-tone finish, 13 single-tone paint options are available. Complementing the bespoke paint options are a set of small 16-inch forged wheels with distinctive center caps. Cavalier also offers the Topolino with a special Night Package that replaces the exposed grey exterior parts with painted black elements.

Cavalier's touches start with the paint. Customers can order their bespoke Topolino in one of ten available two-tone paint schemes, ranging from Ivory White with Sage Green to Deep Black and Deep Bordeaux Red, and our favorite of the bunch: Light Silver Grey with Warm Terracotta Orange. If you don't like the two-tone finish, 13 single-tone paint options are available. Complementing the bespoke paint options are a set of small 16-inch forged wheels with distinctive center caps. Cavalier also offers the Topolino with a special Night Package that replaces the exposed grey exterior parts with painted black elements.

The microcar's interior has also been changed. The seats, steering wheel, door cards, and headliner are now clad in a mix of plush Nappa leather and genuine Alcantara with several color options. The Topolino then benefits from a panoramic glass roof that transitions from clear to opaque as well as leather grab handles, wool floor mats, and configurable ambient lighting. The firm has also added a small 3.7-inch central screen for some added convenience. Usually, a standard Topolino owner has to use their smartphone as the main display. Cavalier is promising a bespoke audio system with Bluetooth for the Topolino, but it hasn't specified how many speakers it includes.

As the standard Fiat Topolino was only designed for inner-city use, it uses a tiny 5.5-kWh lithium-ion battery pack with 47 miles (75 km) of range and a front-mounted electric motor delivering 8 horsepower. Cavalier's version can be configured with a larger 10.8-kWh battery, boosting the microcar's driving range to 93 miles (150 km). Additionally, adjustments made to the vehicle's control unit boost the top speed from just 28 mph (45 km/h) to 43 mph (70 km/h). That's not enough for highway use, but it might be enough to ensure owners don't hold up traffic whenever they get behind the wheel. A 2-kW Webasto diesel heater is an option and should keep the cabin warm without draining the tiny battery pack.

Cavalier's Topolino ticks plenty of boxes for those looking for something small and exclusive. However, it comes at a cost. The Belgian firm says upgrades start at €12,000 ($13,300) for the simplest configuration and rise to about €20,000 ($22,200) for the full package. That's a serious amount of coin, especially since the regular Topolino starts at just under €10,000 ($11,100) in Italy and $13,995 in the United States . All up, you're looking at a tiny two-door that can cost upwards of €30,000 ($33,300) or about the same as a new Honda Civic Hybrid in the U.S.

Taking a friend to court on time is a perfectly reasonable favor. Trying to make up for potentially missing that appointment by testing out the V-max of a Toyota RAV4 on public roads is considerably harder to explain. According to police in Florida, that's exactly what one woman did. Not only did she go to jail, but her court-bound passenger went, too. Hey, at least he ended up in the building he was planning on going to.

As Guessing Headlights first brought to light, the situation went down on October 29. Police said a trooper clocked a 2025 RAV4 at 120 mph on Interstate 95 in Volusia County. That trooper, Rickie R. Zigler, says he accelerated to 131 mph just to catch up. When he did, the RAV4 driver pulled over, and he took her to his car. This is where things go from criminal to somewhat comical and yet not unserious.

That driver, 22-year-old Medjine Carmelie Francois, said one of her passengers was running late for right around its top speed. The trouble with that strategy, other than now making everyone later, is that it drew even more attention to said passenger while also putting Francois in massive legal trouble.

Florida now has a somewhat infamous Super Speeder law that sends anyone caught going over 100 mph or 50 mph above the speed limit to jail. According to the report, passenger Keyshawn Charles Bennett, also 22, had a hearing scheduled just seven minutes after the trooper first spotted the Toyota. He also had two outstanding felony warrants for failing to appear in court in that same case.

Troopers arrested Bennett on those warrants and Francois on a charge of driving at least 50 mph over the limit. Both went to the Volusia County Jail, and the Toyota was towed. Francois' bond was listed at $500, but she's likely on the hook for much more. The RAV4 in question was a rental , and the rental car company doesn't get a special exemption to just go pick it up whenever this sort of thing happens. On top of that, if Francois is convicted, she faces up to 30 days in jail, a $500 fine, or both. Hey, at least we now know the latest RAV4 can hit 120.

This extreme 750S is the work of American firm S Klub LA. The tuner first appeared on our radar a couple of years ago when it unveiled a dramatic speedster version of the legendary Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren. It's now returned with a CLK GTR lookalike. As real CLK GTR models are worth in excess of $10 million, we'd argue modifying a McLaren to look like a CLK GTR is much better than trying to modify and upgrade an original. Still, plenty of people will probably consider this automotive sacrilege.

It appears almost all exterior panels from the donor 750S have been replaced. The front now has quad headlights just like the Mercedes, as well as a sleek black grille, a low-slung bumper, and a black chin spoiler. It also rocks wide front fenders and sits on a set of aero-disc inspired white wheels. Overall, it looks pretty nice from the front.

From the windshield back, the McLaren underpinnings become apparent. The roof looks identical to a regular 750S, and it also appears to have original McLaren door skins. These doors are far more flowing, and much larger, than an original CLK GTR's doors . They're somewhat at odds with the rest of the design. Similarly, the rear quarter panels look just like those of the 750S, but do include flared fenders for that widebody look.

The rear is a little different as very little is shared in common between it and the base car. A new tail has been designed with CLK-inspired taillights, a large lip spoiler, and a fixed carbon fiber rear wing. S-Klub has also crafted a wild carbon diffuser for the supercar. It hasn't bothered trying to replicate the exhausts of the original, and retained the four, central quad exhausts of the McLaren, now with chrome tailpipes.

The 750S's original cabin layout has been retained, as trying to build an interior to mimic the CLK GTR would be extremely laborious and expensive. Some custom touches have been made, including new red leather across the driver's seat, steering wheel, dashboard, and door panel, while the passenger side is bathed in plush quilted white leather.

Plymouth built some memorable cars before it was killed off in 2001, and the strange-looking Prowler was one of the last. Launched in 1997, then axed in 2002 after morphing into a Chrysler, the Prowler was an automotive oddity that didn't deserve all the hate it got .

A particularly pristine 2000 Prowler has just hit the market and it even comes with a matching trailer. The car, listed for sale through Bring a Trailer , has only ever been driven 16,374 miles and remains completely original. You'd be hard-pressed to find another Prowler as good as this one available in the U.S. And cruising down the coastline in this thing with the wind in your hair would certainly be memorable.

The Prowler uses a naturally aspirated 3.5-liter V6 with 253 horsepower and 255 pound-feet of torque. Those were respectable figures back in the day and should still be enough to excite. What's not so exciting is that the Prowler was only ever sold with a four-speed automatic transmission, so a car like this might not appeal to the keenest of driving enthusiasts.

A look at its Carfax report reveals the car was involved in an accident back in 2001 that damaged the left front wheel. It's been repaired and the chrome-finished wheels remain original, as is the Prowler Black paint. Aside from a few scuffs here and there, the car presents well, and has clearly been garaged for most of its life. The interior has also aged rather gracefully. Still present are Agate leather on the seats, off-center gauges, and chrome trimmings around the gear selector. Somehow, the seller has also obtained a small trailer that hooks onto the Prowler, and it comes complete with the same lights as the Plymouth and very similar wheel arches.

As memorable as the Prowler is, it could have been even better. At the 1999 SEMA Show, Plymouth unveiled a special one-off concept car known as the Howler. The Howler ditched the V6 in favor of a naturally aspirated 4.7-liter V8 and added a five-speed manual transmission, morphing it into a legitimate modern hot rod . The Howler was also equipped with a removable hardtop and had a much larger trunk than the Prowler. Not only was it way more powerful, it was also more practical. However, the Prowler was discontinued, and the Howler was never released to the public.

article_paragraphs: Some may remember the ultra-rare electric Chevy S-10 , which was basically an S-10 pickup with GM EV1 running gear. We've seen some versions of the Ranger with an electric shock treatment as well, but not in the cool flareside version known as the Splash. And while it's typically a bad idea to mix electricity and water, this custom EV-converted 1997 Ford Ranger Splash currently for sale on Bring a Trailer is the exception to that rule.

Its bright Canary Yellow paint was an original color for this sporty take on the classic small truck, not a flashy add-on. The original 3.0-liter V6 is gone, replaced with a conversion from Electric Vehicles of America. The Advanced D.C. Motors FB1-4001A motor makes somewhere between 18 and 30 horsepower, a significant downgrade from the original 140 or so from the V6. I know from experience that the V6 wasn't exactly fast, either, so hopefully the instant electric torque makes up for some of the lost power.

The retention of the original five-speed manual transmission is also a nice touch. We've seen this before in EV swaps into vehicles not intended for EV swaps as an easy way to connect the electric motor to the original driveline. According to the instructions taped to the dashboard, there is no clutch, so you just start it in a low gear, then shift to whatever gear best matches your speed. The factory cupholders are still there (which I know from experience will still let your drinks tip over when going around corners at even a moderate speed), and there are three gauges for battery volts (power usage), amps (how much power is left), and a level of charge gauge. There's also a warning light for a hot motor and and on/off switch for the 1,500-watt electric heater, since there's no internal combustion engine to generate heat anymore.

Unlike some modern project EVs , this Ranger followed a simpler approach, which is easier to install and maintain. Rather than a slick Tesla battery pack, it uses a bank of 20 Trojan six-volt batteries, wired in series to produce the 120 volts the motor and Curtis controller need to run the truck. Some of the batteries live in a box between the frame rails, some in the bed like a Cybertruck , and a few under the hood. That's also where the charger lives, so you have to pop the hood to plug it into a standard household outlet. There's no fast charging for this Ranger.

You won't be going very far between charges, either. Electric Vehicles of America estimates the range to be somewhere between 38 and 81 miles, with an average of 53. That's on new batteries, which these are not. EVs have become much more practical in recent years, but the technology in this Ranger is relatively old and crude, so it's pretty much limited to short runs around town between long charging cycles.

If you can live with these limitations, this is actually a great project EV. It's simple enough to be fairly reliable. You can likely maintain it and fix it yourself, and all of the documentation you need is included. It's not perfect, with a torn headliner and some dents and dings around the body, but it's still in good shape for a 1997 Ranger, and easy to fix. It has no reserve and at the time of writing, it has a high bid of $300. I'm sure that will change, but hopefully it will stay less expensive than a Slate truck . Plus, this truck has something no Slate, Cybertruck, or Rivian has: It's a Ford f'in Ranger .

raw_summary: Nissan's very public struggles are well documented , so it shouldn't come as a surprise that the automaker is taking an aggressive stance with its newest and arguably most important model, the Rogue e-Power Hybrid compact crossover. Compact crossover sales account for a massive share of new car sales each year behind only the full-size pickup segment, with heavyweights like the Honda CR-V, Toyota RAV4 , Tesla Model Y , and Nissan Rogue all making the list of the top 10 best-selling cars in the U.S. through Q3 of this year. Our friends at CarsDirect got wind of a dealer bulletin that Nissan sent to its dealers announcing the incentive, which was introduced on November 3 and will run through January 4, 2027.

Our friends at CarsDirect got wind of a dealer bulletin that Nissan sent to its dealers announcing the incentive, which was introduced on November 3 and will run through January 4, 2027.

In order to qualify for the $1,500 trade-in bonus, interested shoppers must have a 2021-or-newer Toyota RAV4 that they trade in when purchasing or leasing a 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid. The deal is transferable to members of the same household, and it can be stacked with Nissan's other current offers. Those other offers include a financing deal of 4.9% APR for 60 months, and a lease deal on the west coast where lessees pay $439 per month for 36 months with $4,959 due at signing and a mileage limit of 10,000 miles per year.

Jalopnik's own Andy Kalmowitz sampled the 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid at the first drive event in Santa Barbara, California, late last month which you can check out here , and he preferred driving the new Rogue Hybrid over the new Toyota RAV4 hybrid.

The 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid features a unique series hybrid drivetrain that operates primarily as an EV. The turbocharged 1.5-liter three-cylinder engine under the hood is solely responsible for charging the Rogue's 1.67-kWh battery, and is not connected to the wheels. The wheels are driven by electric motors mounted on the front and rear axles providing standard all-wheel-drive, and they're capable of scooting the Rogue from 0-to-60 in a quick 6.4 seconds without ever needing to be plugged in. It's rated for 41 mpg in the city, 36 mpg on the highway, and 38 mpg combined which is slightly worse than the RAV4 hybrid, but Andy says the Rogue's interior is a much more comfortable and luxurious space than the RAV4 provides.

BMW’s electric vehicle lineup will look much different in 2027. The German luxury automaker is shaking things up with the arrival of its Neue Klasse EVs, bringing significantly longer ranges, faster charging times, and advanced new tech and features.
To sweeten the deal, BMW launched a new public charging promotion on Thursday for eligible model-year 2027 electric vehicles, including the new iX3, i5, and i7.

The new BMW ChargingNetwork package provides $500 in total credits. $300 of which includes a BMW ChargingNetwork credit that can be used at one of 15 public charging providers, such as ChargePoint, EVgo, Shell Recharge, and IONNA. The other $200 is for IONNA locations only.
On top of this, the promo includes a free one-year BMW Membership at IONNA. The membership provides a 25% discount on charging during the free year trial.
BMW said the charging credits will automatically apply after you enroll in the BMW ChargingNetwork.

You can enroll through the My BMW app. Under Charging, select Services, then Charging Wallet, and then BMW ChargingNetwork. Once complete, the credits and other benefits will show up in the Digital Charging Wallet and will be automatically applied to eligible charging sessions.
Which one to choose? The 2027 iX3 is BMW’s first Neue Klasse vehicle. Based on its sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive, the iX3 delivers an EPA-estimated range of up to 434 miles.

article_paragraphs: Ferrari F1 chief Fred Vasseur insists he has cleared the air with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton after their highly publicised Mexican Grand Prix clash last week.

At the Mexico City event, Hamilton and Leclerc both went off track on lap one as they fought for the lead, with Hamilton losing a position to Max Verstappen instead, while Leclerc was penalised and eventually also ceded the lead to the Red Bull driver.

Verstappen went on to win the race with Hamilton second and Leclerc off the podium in fourth, with the sabre-rattling on lap one robbing the team of a possible third win of the campaign. Hamilton was particularly furious about how Leclerc had raced him at the start, lobbying for the stewards to hand his team-mate a bigger penalty for cutting the track.

The seven-time world champion demanded serious talks with Leclerc and Vasseur over how hard his team-mate was racing him, while Vasseur was frustrated with what he felt was a lack of respect towards Maranello's 2,000-strong staff trying to provide both drivers with a winning car.

Those talks have since happened on Thursday night in Sao Paulo, and speaking to the media for the first time since last weekend, Vasseur was adamant the message to both of his drivers was loud and clear. Ferrari must always come first.

"The guidelines are always the same. They are two competitors with a fighting spirit for sure, but they need to have respect for each other," Vasseur said. "But mainly and firstly, they need to respect the brand, the team, the people working at home, the people working on track. I think we are putting a lot of effort on this and the message was clear and will stay clear."

On Thursday Hamilton said he agreed with suggestions that Leclerc was racing him harder than he raced other drivers, his team boss pointed towards Leclerc's aggressive overtake on Verstappen in Austin to downplay those claims.

"He said that he was fighting probably a bit harder with him than with some others, but if you have a look at what Charles did in Austin in the first sector, everybody said that it was magic," Vasseur said. "The line is fine between the two. But he didn't crash into the other car."

title: U.S. Automakers Still Pushing For Complete Ban Of Chinese Cars

article_paragraphs: The potential for Chinese automakers to sell cars in America is something we've talked about all year long. Just a year or so ago, it seemed like an impossibility. Today, everything is flipped on its head and domestic automakers are so afraid of having to compete that they're begging lawmakers to make sure the market is anything but free to Chinese companies.

According to Reuters , the Alliance for Automotive Innovation renewed that call on Monday. Its membership includes Ford and GM alongside Toyota, Volkswagen, Hyundai, and other foreign brands with a stake in the American market. The group's president, John Bozzella, urged Congress to "stop Chinese automakers from doing here what they've gotten away with in Europe."

He pointed to EU imports of more than 1.1 million Chinese-built vehicles during the first eight months of 2026, exceeding the total for all of 2025. The argument basically breaks into two major categories. First, concerns over privacy and vehicle surveillance. Secondly, a desire to insulate domestic automakers from having to compete with a product that is vastly cheaper and, in many ways, more sophisticated.

In case anyone forgot. Chinese automakers already don't sell cars in America. There are tariffs that keep those automakers and plenty of others out of the country. In January 2025, the Biden administration finalized connected-vehicle restrictions targeting certain Chinese and Russian technology, as well as manufacturers with sufficient ties to either country.

Software restrictions and the prohibition on covered manufacturers selling new connected vehicles take effect for the 2027 model year. Restrictions covering vehicle-connectivity hardware follow for the 2030 model year, with a separate January 2029 deadline for hardware without an associated model year. Importantly, these restrictions apply even when a vehicle is built in the USA. It's what has basically kicked Polestar out of the country. And Congress could make barriers like that more durable.

The Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 , sponsored by Republican Bernie Moreno and Democrat Elissa Slotkin, would put restrictions into federal law. It advanced unanimously from the Senate Commerce Committee in July, so it's already got some support. It covers connected vehicles, specified software, and connectivity hardware associated with countries of concern. It also targets attempts to bypass the restrictions by renaming, rebranding, or restructuring covered products.

Of course, President Donald Trump could nix the entire thing via a veto if he wants to. He said in September that he'd be open to Chinese cars in America so long as they're built stateside. Automakers wouldn't love that. Lawmakers might not either. But the folks paying over $50,000 on average for a new car might not be too dismayed.

article_paragraphs: Police have a tough job no matter where they serve. That job gets considerably tougher when the person they're chasing can move much faster. This pursuit in the U.K. didn't begin with a roaring V8, flashing lights, or some impressive driving. There wasn't even an engine involved. An officer on foot was trying to catch a suspected thief who was fleeing from police on a bicycle, and he managed it thanks to a good Samaritan in a van, of all things.

According to Guildford Beat (Surrey Police) , officers were on Woking Road in Guildford, England, when they spotted someone suspected of stealing from a nearby shop. The suspect took off on a bicycle — a regular one, not a 70-mph e-bike – leaving Police Constable Sperling to give chase on foot.

Police shared bodycam video footage on November 4 showing the cyclist, dressed in gray, riding away as the officer follows. For a few moments, PC Sperling is close enough to get a good look at him, but that's a lot different than being able to keep up. As the gap began to grow, a good Samaritan stepped in with the hero of this story ... a van.

The police clearly had some fun putting this clip together. As the cyclist pulls away, a caption announces that he's getting away before the video cuts to a black screen. Anyone expecting that to be the end gets a quick correction: "Just kidding!"

That's where the van enters the picture. Its driver stops to offer Sperling a lift, and the officer climbs into the passenger side. The pair trundle off at the van's fastest pace, which, admittedly, isn't exactly quick. But it's quite a bit faster than any cyclist can manage, and these folks weren't exactly chasing down Lance Armstrong on performance-enhancing drugs.

From inside the cab, the footage shows the officer pointing as the pair continue along the road. Police say the driver and Sperling worked together to spot where the cyclist had gone and get ahead of him. Once in position, Sperling popped out of the van like part of the A-Team. Sperling's bodycam captures the moments when the officer gets ahead of the rider and tackles him to the ground. Police confirmed the arrest, thanked the van driver for their help, but didn't identify the rider.

Most of the time, a van is basically a box on wheels , and would be somewhere near the bottom of our list of vehicles to use in a police chase. In this rare instance, it was perfect for the job. After all, the person trying to get away was still relying on his own legs.

article_paragraphs: Remember when electromods were all the rage at SEMA? If you do, you might recall that Stellantis revealed a classic 1967 Plymouth GTX muscle car at the 2024 show , whose V8 heart had been swapped for an electric powertrain. Turns out the guy who sold Stellantis the car was less than impressed, so this year the brand righted that wrong with a Hellcrate apology.

"We heard him, so this year we fixed it," Stellantis American brands boss, and confirmed V8 flag flier, Tim Kuniskis said. "We put a supercharged Hemi back under the hood, and I have a feeling he's going to like this version a whole lot better."

The GTX arrived for 1967 as Plymouth's rival to the Pontiac GTO that had been raising hell, and ton of cash, for GM since 1964. It looked pretty low key, hailing from a time before bright colors, bold graphics and fledgling spoilers began to dominate the muscle car scene. But there's nothing meek about this SEMA GTX. It's finished in Frostbite Blue metallic and rides on 18-inch BTG Vintage Bronze forged magnesium wheels, just as it did at SEMA two years ago. But now the hood features twin silver racing stripes, and has a scoop that looks like it could suck birds right out of the sky.

Air rushing into that scoop feeds a Hellcrate Redeye 6.2-liter supercharged Hemi crate engine package, one of the powertrain options Stellantis announced at this year's event. It makes 885 hp (897 PS) and up to 787 lb ft (1,067 Nm) of torque in high octane mode, and drives the rear wheels via a TorqueFlite 8HP90 eight-speed automatic transmission. That compares with a feeble 335 hp (340 PS) for the old SEMA '24 EV setup.

The GTX was no slouch when new. The base engine was a massive 440 cu in (7.2-liter) Super Commando V8 that thumped out 375 gross horsepower (380 PS), and a fat 480 lb-ft (651 Nm) of torque. And the legendary 426 cu in (7.0-liter) Hemi and its 425 hp (431 PS) and 490 lb-ft (664 Nm), was ready and waiting on the option sheet for street racers who were committed to their craft.

In November 1966, Car and Driver took a 440 — with skinny bias-ply tires and a three-speed automatic — to 60 mph in 6.0 seconds. And the Hemi was faster still. But both would have their work cut out against a restomod packing one of the six Stellantis crate V8s. You've been able to buy modern Hemi crate engines for a while, but this year, Stellantis has bundled them in with a matching engine controller creating simple turnkey solutions for shops and DIYers to put a Hemi, or supercharged Hellcat V8, in their builds.
"Our philosophy is simple: one part, one solution," Kuniskis said at SEMA. "If you're going to build something serious, you shouldn't have to guess whether all the pieces are going to work together."

The new Stellantis crate options start with a base 345 Street Strip package that displaces 345 cubes (5.7-liter) and makes 385 hp (390 PS) and 417 lb-ft (565 Nm). A gutsier 392 cu in (6.4-liter) version ups the ante to 485 hp (492 PS) and 475 lb-ft (644 Nm), and after that you're into supercharged territory. King of the crates is the 376 cu in (6.2-liter) Hellephant Super Stock, which generates a monstrous 1,025 hp (1,039 PS) and 945 lb-ft (1,281 Nm). So how brave are you feeling?

This hypercar’s cabin also positions all of its key controls around the driver and minimizes distractions by forgoing traditional infotainment and driver-assistance features altogether. title: Think The Last VW Beetle Was Retro Enough? Hurtan Didn't, So They Built This
raw_summary: When Volkswagen discontinued the Beetle, it effectively removed retro design from the lineup. Still, an unnamed Beetle owner in Germany thought that the original could use an extra dose of vintage styling, and commissioned Spanish coachbuilder Hurtan Automobiles to create a one-off. The unique creation is based on the A5 generation of the iconic VW Beetle Cabriolet that remained in production between 2011 and 2019. However, the model is virtually unrecognizable due to custom body panels covering most of its surfaces. In fact, the only carry-over bits appear to be the greenhouse, mirrors, door cards, rear quarter panels, and fabric retractable roof. The Beetle already came with bulbous fenders from the factory, but Hurtan took it to another level by extending them into the front doors. The fenders carry a set of round halogen headlights, and are combined with a bespoke front bumper and Bentley-style grille featuring gold accents and the Hurtan emblem. Other highlights include additional lights mounted next to the license plate, and the hood recess which is purely cosmetic.

The Beetle already came with bulbous fenders from the factory, but Hurtan took it to another level by extending them into the front doors. The fenders carry a set of round halogen headlights, and are combined with a bespoke front bumper and Bentley-style grille featuring gold accents and the Hurtan emblem. Other highlights include additional lights mounted next to the license plate, and the hood recess which is purely cosmetic.

Moving to the back, the rear overhang has been extended, making room for swooping rear fenders and a pronounced bumper inspired by classic cars of the '40s . The model also rocks a larger tailgate with an integrated third brake light, two-story taillights, and aftermarket alloy wheels with five double spokes. While Hurtan didn't share photos of the interior, it appears that the one-off has gained light-colored upholstery.

We can also see what looks like the stock infotainment display mounted on the dashboard. The Granada-based company confirmed that the build retains the modern VW Group platform, safety systems, and running gear of the donor vehicle beneath the vintage shell. This suggests that the coachbuilt special is powered by one of the stock TSI or TDI units available for the last Beetle.

Hurtan shared the photos on its official Facebook page without revealing the cost of the conversion. Still, we all know that one-off commissions usually require a hefty investment. Interestingly, this is not the first time the Spanish company got their hands on a retro-flavored model, as it has created builds based on the Chrysler PT Cruiser Convertible and Jeep Wrangler. Still, its most famous project remains the Miata-based Grand Albaycín.

In a recent nationally representative survey , BMW found that Americans want more EV range than they actually need.
The study found that 73% consider 75 miles of range, or less, enough to cover their daily driving. Meanwhile, 42% said they would require at least 300 miles of range to consider an EV.
Another 53% said they would be more likely to consider an EV if it could add about 150 miles of range in 10 minutes.
BMW’s new iX3 checks all the boxes. Based on BMW’s sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive 800V system, the 2027 iX3 50 xDrive delivers an EPA-estimated range of up to 434 miles (with 20″ summer tires).
With the 22″ summer tires, the iX3 50 xDrive has an EPA-estimated range of up to 392 miles. Still, plenty for at least a week of commuting.
It can also add 170-185 miles of range in 10 minutes with up to 400 kW DC fast charging. In everyday, real-world driving, it may drive even further than its official EPA numbers suggest.
During Edmunds ‘ EV Range test , the 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive (with 22″ summer tires) drove 436 miles on a single charge, topping its EPA estimate of 392 miles by 44 miles.

raw_title: Tesla Swears Cybercab Meets Federal Safety Standards, But Doesn't Want You To Know How
title: Tesla Swears Cybercab Meets Federal Safety Standards, But Doesn't Want You To Know How
raw_summary: The Cybercab is an ambitious project for Tesla. It aims to achieve full autonomy, become the next big thing in robotaxis, and do it all without a steering wheel and pedals. The car is so ambitious, in fact, that on the day it launched, the NHTSA immediately began an investigation , wondering how Tesla could certify it for road use without those controls. Now, Tesla has answered the NHTSA — more formally, the National Highway Transportation Safety Administration — but the company really doesn't want you to know what it said. As we initially reported, Tesla had until September 30 to respond to the NHTSA's questions. It requested an eight-week extension, and the administration split the difference and told it to answer instead by October 30. That date has come and gone, and sure enough, the automaker did respond. The tricky part is that in its public response, Tesla offered one whole sentence. "The entirety of this file is confidential business information." That's right: Nothing to see here, folks. Move it along.

article_paragraphs: The Cybercab is an ambitious project for Tesla. It aims to achieve full autonomy, become the next big thing in robotaxis, and do it all without a steering wheel and pedals. The car is so ambitious, in fact, that on the day it launched, the NHTSA immediately began an investigation , wondering how Tesla could certify it for road use without those controls. Now, Tesla has answered the NHTSA — more formally, the National Highway Transportation Safety Administration — but the company really doesn't want you to know what it said.

As we initially reported, Tesla had until September 30 to respond to the NHTSA's questions. It requested an eight-week extension, and the administration split the difference and told it to answer instead by October 30. That date has come and gone, and sure enough, the automaker did respond. The tricky part is that in its public response, Tesla offered one whole sentence. "The entirety of this file is confidential business information." That's right: Nothing to see here, folks. Move it along.

The wildest part is that all of this is happening because automakers like Tesla get to self-certify that their cars meet or exceed Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. The September 10 Special Order from the NHTSA to Tesla included 21 requests about how it certified the Cybercab. Each is something Tesla must reply to, and do it under oath. Some of the questions here explain why the NHTSA has a bee in its bonnet.

For example, at one point, the order questions how Tesla met FMVSS 135, which states, "The service brakes shall be activated by means of a foot control." That seems kinda tough considering that the automaker is pretty open about it not having a foot control. Who knows? Maybe there's something hidden we don't know about, or maybe Tesla has a creative answer for that question.

The agency also wants to know about things like mirrors, turn signals that cancel through steering wheel rotation, and whether Tesla used temporary controls to certify the car. If it did, it could fly in the face of other regulations that say the automaker can't disable required safety equipment. The entire thing seems quite sticky for Tesla, and the fact that it doesn't want to release its answers to the public casts its own odd shadow on the operation.

While it said basically nothing in one filing, Tesla did release a 30-page Cybercab first responder document in which it describes the car as "Not typically equipped with a steering wheel or acceleration and brake pedals." Is that an admission that one can install temporary controls when they want? We might not ever know. What is clear from the document is that first responders do have a way to move the car.

Evidently, they can show their badge to the camera in the B-pillar of the car, a Tesla rep can verify their credentials, and then a set of controls will pop up on the infotainment screen. Those controls don't make up for the lack of physical controls that the NHTSA is asking about , but hey, at least it's something.

For now, we'll just have to wait to see what happens next. If the administration accepts Tesla's arguments, it's possible the document never comes to light. If the NHTSA disagrees that the information is confidential business information, it has the right to make it public. That would certainly be interesting.

Most of the reason the Brick Shop team has managed to get the rollout right with a mix of obvious heroes like the Lamborghini Miura and secret-enthusiast-handshake cars like the Audi RS2 is down to close work with the designers at Hot Wheels. Located in El Segundo, California, the Hot Wheels team members are all gearheads of one flavor or another, and the passion they have for all wheeled things is genuine. Just, you know, scaled down for those iconic orange tracks.

Small scale is where you’ll find the latest Mattel Bricks sets, now built to the same size as the roughly 1/64th scale Hot Wheels themselves. They’re simple little cars, fewer than 30 pieces per kit, and at $4.99 each, they’re as dangerously tempting as an open family-size bag of potato chips. You can’t just have one.

The launch sets include a 2018 Audi TT RS , a 1991 Acura NSX , a 2024 Chevrolet Camaro ZL1 , a Maserati MCPura , a 1999 Honda S2000 , and a Bone Shaker (a 20-year-old hot rod by Hot Wheels design legend Larry Wood). The sets will be sold in blind boxes, so you’ll be getting a car at random when you’re buying them, adding to the fun. Launch is planned for January of next year, so you’ll be able to get your hands on one even if Santa pegged you on the naughty list for doing burnouts.

Even better is that these six tiny cars are only the first wave. By the end of next year, Mattel plans to have 20 models of 1/64-scale cars, making getting the full lineup something of a challenge for collectors. Even if you’re less serious about completing the series, one or two of these things are surely going to “accidentally” fall into the cart when you next go shopping for groceries.

Caleb Miller began blogging about cars at 13 years old, and he realized his dream of writing for a car magazine after graduating from Carnegie Mellon University and joining the Car and Driver team. He loves quirky and obscure autos, aiming to one day own something bizarre like a Nissan S-Cargo, and is an avid motorsports fan.

raw_title: Mercedes May Delay U.S. Production Of The GLC Until 2030
title: Mercedes May Delay U.S. Production Of The GLC Until 2030
raw_summary: Mercedes-Benz confirmed earlier this year that it would start building the popular GLC in the United States , allowing it to avoid tariffs when importing the current model from Europe. Though the German automaker never gave a firm date as to when American production of the GLC would start, it has reportedly delayed these plans by more than two years. Unnamed sources have revealed to Auto News that U.S. production of the GLC may not start until May 2030, well beyond forecasts that had indicated assembly could start in late 2027. No explanation has been given for the reported delay, though Mercedes will certainly feel the impact on its bottom line. The automaker sold almost 54,000 examples of the GLC through the first nine months of 2026 in the U.S., and more than 71,000 total in 2025. The SUV is currently built in Europe and subject to 15% tariffs . One possible explanation for the update in manufacturing plans is a report that the tariff rate could be cut to 10% by the U.S. Commerce Department, a change that would save Mercedes millions of dollars. If that happens, Mercedes may lose the impetus to fast-track North American GLC production.

If that happens, Mercedes may lose the impetus to fast-track North American GLC production.

The German brand currently operates an important manufacturing facility in Alabama, where it builds the GLE, GLE Coupe, and GLS. Earlier this year, the plant built its 5 millionth vehicle, and Mercedes has committed to investing more than $7 billion in its U.S. operations by 2030, showing just how serious it is about American production. Of this investment, $4 billion will be directed specifically to the Alabama site.

If reports about the GLC's American production future are true, it's unlikely the current-generation model will be produced locally. Mercedes launched the second-gen GLC in 2022, and analysts don't think it'd make sense to build this model in the U.S. After all, it'll be eight years old by 2030. As a result, it's more likely the next-generation version will be the one manufactured in North America. Very little is known about this new model, but we believe it will retain a large selection of combustion and hybrid powertrains, while continuing to offer an all-electric GLC variant.

title: If You Love Ferrari, Then You Need Its Customer-Spec Le Mans Racer
raw_summary: One of the rarest and most valuable limited-edition Ferraris of the modern era is heading to auction next month, and it could sell for over $9 million. It's the Italian brand's wild 499P Modificata , launched a few years ago as a customer-spec version of the 24 Hours of Le Mans-winning 499P. If you want the ultimate track-day toy, then this is it. The Modificata is based on the same Dallara chassis as the endurance racer and also uses the same twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter V6 and front-mounted electric motor. Because it doesn't have to comply with racing regulations, it delivers a combined 858 horsepower with the 161 hp Push to Pass system enabled. To put that figure into perspective, racing regulations cap the Le Mans winner at 680 hp.

It's the Italian brand's wild 499P Modificata , launched a few years ago as a customer-spec version of the 24 Hours of Le Mans-winning 499P. If you want the ultimate track-day toy, then this is it.

The Modificata is based on the same Dallara chassis as the endurance racer and also uses the same twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter V6 and front-mounted electric motor. Because it doesn't have to comply with racing regulations, it delivers a combined 858 horsepower with the 161 hp Push to Pass system enabled. To put that figure into perspective, racing regulations cap the Le Mans winner at 680 hp.

Ferrari made several other upgrades to the customer car. For example, important suspension components, electronic controls, and the engine maps have been modified, and the Michelin tires of the race car have been replaced with a bespoke set of Pirellis. Like the race car, the 499P Modificata's body is made from lightweight carbon fiber, and it has all of the same aero appendages, making track-focused Ferraris like the SF90 XX Stradale and 296 Speciale seem a little restrained.

The Italian brand has never actually disclosed how many 499P Modificata models exist, although there are known to be at least 30 in existence. Christie's is auctioning what appears to be the first unit to hit the used car market, and believes it will sell for over 7.5 million Swiss francs or just over $9 million.

This one is chassis number 20 and is painted in red with white '88' roundels on the front and the colors of the Italian flag running along the sides. The next owner will gain access to Ferrari's ultra-exclusive Sport Prototipo Clienti program that runs exclusive track days for 499P Modificata owners and provides technical support and maintenance for all the cars. This car must remain at Ferrari's Maranello facilities until December 2028, where it will be stored and maintained. Only after that date can the next owner add the car to their personal collection.

title: As Jackery Inventory Sells Out, Are Portable Batteries Set To Take Off?
raw_summary: I recently wrote reviews of the new Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 and Explorer 100D . A few days later, a connection with Jackery messaged me that their Black Friday/Cyber Monday products had largely sold out. Just three days after launching on November 1. This includes 1000, 2000, 3600 and 5000 portable power and solar generator models. Additional models have sold out since then or will likely sell out soon. The recently launched Explorer 100D is still available in limited quantities at Walmart and Costco. While Jackery will still take orders for Black Friday/Cyber Monday sales, most models currently listed for purchase will be on a preorder basis. Customers should check estimated delivery dates. Some restocking is expected in late November, although broader inventory availability may not recover until early next year.
