article_paragraphs: Mahindra Auto recently launched the XUV3XO ZNG in the country and we drove it in Mumbai last month at the media drive . Mahindra promised that XUV3XO ZNG will not differ much from the Bharat NCAP safety ratings of non-CNG Petrol-Only XUV3XO. Within a month of that promise, Mahindra has delivered.

XUV3XO ZNG Bharat NCAP crash ratings are out and it scores exactly the same as the Petrol-only model. The additional weight of the CNG and all the structural modifications to the platform to accommodate the dual-cylinder CNG storage solution has not affected XUV3XO’s basic crash performance in any way.

Bharat NCAP crash testing agency has just published the crash testing results of Mahindra XUV3XO ZNG and it is now the latest vehicle in India to score the prestigious 5 Star crash safety rating. XUV3XO ZNG comes with over 35 standard safety features including 6 airbags, ISOFIX mounts, ESC and even dedicated CNG safety features.

With this achievement, Mahindra XUV3XO ZNG becomes India’s first Sub 4m CNG SUV to achieve this milestone. Where ratings are concerned, XUV3XO ZNG was subjected to Bharat NCAP’s usual crash testing norms and it scored 29.3 / 32 points in adult occupant protection and 45 / 49 points in child occupant protection.

On Bharat NCAP’s website, Mahindra XUV3XO ZNG is not listed as a separate car which underwent a crash test. Instead, the crash performance results of XUV3XO are extended to ZNG variants as well. The PM CG MT CNG Family which now gets 5 Star crash safety rating include MX1, MX2, MX Edge, REVX Edge (O), AX5 and REVX A.

Mahindra XUV3XO ZNG comes equipped with dual-cylinder CNG storage solution that ensures that boot space is not compromised like it usually happens in a single-cylinder solution. It is commendable that Mahindra has also retained the spare wheel under the body and then the same performance as non-CNG Petrol-only counterpart.

Dr Velusamy R, President, Automotive Business, Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd., said, “At Mahindra, safety is a fundamental commitment that guides every stage of vehicle development. The XUV 3XO ZNG was engineered to excel across every aspect of the ownership experience, delivering ‘zero compromise’ in space, technology, performance and driving experience.

Its robust architecture is engineered to provide high levels of occupant protection and peace of mind on every journey. The 5-star Bharat NCAP rating is a testament to our engineering excellence and reinforces the XUV 3XO ZNG’s position as an SUV that excels across every dimension.”

article_paragraphs: Hero MotoCorp has launched Xtreme 125R Stealth Edition with TFT at Rs 1,16,250 (ex-showroom). Positioned as the new top-spec variant , it brings additional technology and exclusive styling to the sporty 125cc motorcycle.

Key highlights include a 4.2-inch TFT display, Tyre Pressure Monitoring System (TPMS), Bluetooth connectivity and a new colour scheme. The Stealth Edition costs Rs 6,700 more than the existing Dual Channel ABS variant, priced at Rs 1,09,550.

The biggest upgrade is a new 4.2-inch TFT instrument cluster with Bluetooth connectivity. It supports turn-by-turn navigation, incoming call and SMS alerts, and music controls, offering greater convenience for daily commuting.

Another important addition is TPMS, which Hero claims is a segment-first feature in the sporty 125cc motorcycle category. It provides real-time tyre pressure readings and alerts riders when pressure requires attention.

The Stealth Edition also comes equipped with dual-channel ABS, three riding modes – Rain, Road and Sport – and cruise control. These features make it one of the more comprehensively equipped motorcycles in the 125cc segment.

Hero has introduced a Midnight Black colour scheme with Pearl Red accents for the Stealth Edition. Coloured alloy wheels further distinguish it from regular variants. The overall design remains unchanged, retaining the angular headlamp, sharp fuel tank extensions, split-seat setup and sporty bodywork.

Existing Xtreme 125R variants are offered in multiple colours, including Firestorm Red, Cobalt Blue, Stallion Black, Abrax Orange, Black Moon Yellow, Black Cocktail Blue and Black Leaf Green. The Dual Channel ABS variant also gets Black Pearl Red and Black Matshadow Gray.

Mechanically, Xtreme 125R continues with its 124.7cc, single-cylinder, air-cooled, fuel-injected engine producing 11.4 bhp at 8,250 rpm and 10.5 Nm at 6,500 rpm, paired with a 5-speed gearbox. Hero claims 0-60 km/h acceleration in 5.7 seconds and fuel efficiency of 66 km/l.

raw_title: New Renault Duster Strong Hybrid Customer Deliveries Begin In India
title: New Renault Duster Strong Hybrid Customer Deliveries Begin In India
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The handover to first Renault Duster E-Tech hybrid customer took place in Hyderabad on November 6 coinciding with the inauguration of a new showroom Renault India has commenced customer deliveries of the Duster Strong Hybrid E-Tech 160 – nearly three weeks after introducing the SUV on October 17. The first handover took place at a newly inaugurated dealership in Hitec City, Hyderabad today. The city is among the Indian markets recording the highest bookings for the petrol/electric Duster. The hybrid also becomes the first Renault vehicle sold in India to use the company’s E-Tech self-charging powertrain. The delivery commencement coincides with Renault’s plans to modernise its dealership network in India. The manufacturer intends to convert all 73 showrooms in its 24 popular cities to the new retail format by July 2027. These cities contribute nearly half of Renault India sales and 30 outlets have already received the revised showroom treatment. The company also operates nearly 638 sales and service touchpoints nationwide comprising more than 200 Workshop on Wheels locations. The Duster Strong Hybrid E-Tech 160 is available in Evolution, Techno and Emotion variants. Prices start at Rs. 16.99 lakh for the Evolution and rise to Rs. 19.49 lakh (both prices, ex-showroom) for the top-spec Emotion. The introductory prices are applicable to vehicles delivered until December 31, 2026. Customers who purchased the Renault R-Pass receive priority allocation while regular bookings are available for Rs. 21,000. Variant Price (ex-showroom) Renault Duster E-Tech 160 Evolution Rs. 16.99 lakh Renault Duster E-Tech 160 Techno Rs. 18.99 lakh Renault Duster E-Tech 160 Emotion Rs. 19.49 lakh The hybrid powertrain uses a 1.8-litre naturally aspirated four-cylinder petrol engine, two electric motors, and a 1.4 kWh lithium-ion battery. The combined output stands at 160 PS while the electric traction motor develops 208 Nm of torque. A multimode automatic transmission manages power delivery. Renault claims acceleration from 0 to 100 kmph in 9.6 seconds. The battery receives electricity from regenerative braking and the petrol engine and thus external charging is unnecessary. The first customer received the SUV from Francisco Hidalgo, Vice President of Sales and Marketing at Renault Group India. The vehicle was handed over to T. Krishna Gopal, CEO of Eduzi Academy, at the new Hyderabad showroom. The facility occupies 7,000 square feet and has space to display eight cars making it Renault’s largest showroom in the city. The dealership is operated by VVC Group which now manages three Renault showrooms and two workshops in Hyderabad. The Duster hybrid features an illuminated Duster emblem on the grille, E-Tech badges, LED headlamps and a horizontal LED rear light bar. The SUV also gets 212 mm of ground clearance and 18-inch wheels. On the inside, selected variants receive a 10.1-inch infotainment touchscreen, a 10.25-inch digital instrument cluster, a panoramic sunroof, ventilated front seats, and dual-zone climate control. Six airbags are standard while the remaining equipment varies according to the chosen trim. Renault claims an ARAI-certified fuel efficiency of 29 kmpl and a driving range of more than 1,400 km under specified conditions. The company also states that electric propulsion can handle up to 80 per cent of city driving time under suitable circumstances. The Duster Strong Hybrid competes against the Maruti Suzuki Grand Vitara, Maruti Suzuki Victoris and Toyota Urban Cruiser Hyryder hybrid models.

title: Energica rises from the ashes with plans for cheaper electric motorcycles
raw_summary: The Italian electric motorcycle maker, which ceased operations in 2024 after entering judicial liquidation, has announced a major revival under new international ownership. And while the Energica name is returning, the company behind it is going to look quite different this time around. Perhaps the biggest change is where the motorcycles will actually be built.
summary: The Italian electric motorcycle maker, which ceased operations in 2024 after entering judicial liquidation, has announced a major revival under new international ownership. And while the Energica name is returning, the company behind it is going to look quite different this time around. Perhaps the biggest change is where the motorcycles will actually be built.
article_paragraphs: The Italian electric motorcycle maker, which ceased operations in 2024 after entering judicial liquidation, has announced a major revival under new international ownership. And while the Energica name is returning, the company behind it is going to look quite different this time around.
Perhaps the biggest change is where the motorcycles will actually be built.

Energica says motorcycle production is moving to Asia, while design, engineering, research and development, as well as responsibility for technical and quality standards, will remain in Italy. The new manufacturing setup is expected to significantly reduce production costs, allowing Energica to cut motorcycle prices by around 20% compared to its previous models.
That could be a big deal for a company whose motorcycles were widely praised for their performance and technology, but were also firmly positioned at the premium end of the market.

The revival comes after Energica was acquired by Energica Pte. Ltd. , a Singapore-based company backed by international private investors. Importantly, much of the technological know-how isn’t disappearing overseas with the manufacturing. Energica says its core engineering and design leadership remains in Italy, including longtime CTO Giampiero Testoni and designer Paolo Imeni.

The first motorcycle to make its comeback will be the Energica Experia , the company’s adventure-oriented electric sport-tourer. After that, Energica plans to progressively restart production of the Ego, Eva Ribelle, and EsseEsse9, eventually bringing its entire previous lineup back to market.

At least initially, those motorcycles will use their existing platforms, which should help Energica get bikes rolling off the production line faster without having to develop and homologate entirely new machines. But upgrades are already planned, including a new battery and improvements to range, efficiency, performance, and reliability.

Energica is also specifically targeting Europe, the United States, and Australia as it rebuilds its dealer and service networks. Existing owners haven’t been forgotten either. The company says service has already resumed and spare-parts shipments have restarted to dealers in several countries.

title: Honda Rebel 300 India Specs Revealed - 27.6 PS, 24.5 Nm, 173 Kg, 11.2 L Tank, 690 mm Seat Ht
raw_summary: Launched in August 2026 at Rs 2.22 lakh for the standard variant and Rs 2.62 lakh for the E-Clutch version, both ex-showroom, the Rebel 300 had been awaiting detailed India-specific specifications. The wait is now over. Honda has officially revealed the India-spec Rebel 300’s technical specifications on its website, revealing its power output, weight, dimensions and equipment as customer deliveries approach. The update comes after the first motorcycles began reaching BigWing dealerships earlier this month. Hat tip to automotive enthusiast Ajendra for sharing this update.
summary: Launched in August 2026 at Rs 2.22 lakh for the standard variant and Rs 2.62 lakh for the E-Clutch version, both ex-showroom, the Rebel 300 had been awaiting detailed India-specific specifications. The wait is now over. Honda has officially revealed the India-spec Rebel 300’s technical specifications on its website, revealing its power output, weight, dimensions and equipment as customer deliveries approach.
article_paragraphs: Launched in August 2026 at Rs 2.22 lakh for the standard variant and Rs 2.62 lakh for the E-Clutch version, both ex-showroom, the Rebel 300 had been awaiting detailed India-specific specifications. The wait is now over.

Honda has officially revealed the India-spec Rebel 300’s technical specifications on its website, revealing its power output, weight, dimensions and equipment as customer deliveries approach. The update comes after the first motorcycles began reaching BigWing dealerships earlier this month. Hat tip to automotive enthusiast Ajendra for sharing this update.

Honda lists the Rebel 300 with a 286.01cc, liquid-cooled, single-cylinder, fuel-injected engine producing 20.3 kW, equivalent to approximately 27.6 PS, at 8,000 rpm. Peak torque is rated at 24.5 Nm at 6,250 rpm. Both variants get a six-speed gearbox. The standard motorcycle features an assist and slipper clutch, while the higher-priced version adds Honda’s E-Clutch system.

This allows riders to start, stop and change gears without using the clutch lever, although gear selection still requires the foot-operated shifter. Riders can also use the clutch lever conventionally. The E-Clutch variant weighs 176 kg, making it 3 kg heavier than the 173 kg standard version. Both have an 11.2-litre fuel tank.

Honda Rebel 300 measures 2,200 mm in length, 808 mm in width and 1,125 mm in height, with a 1,506 mm wheelbase. Seat height is confirmed at 690 mm, while ground clearance stands at 129 mm. The low seat should help riders place their feet on the ground, although clearance over taller speed breakers will need consideration.
Suspension comprises telescopic front forks and twin rear shock absorbers. The motorcycle uses 16-inch wheels, with a 130/90 front tyre and a 150/80 rear tyre. Honda also confirms dual-channel ABS.

The equipment list includes LED headlamps and tail lamps, a TFT instrument display, Bluetooth connectivity, turn-by-turn navigation and a Type-C charging port. The TFT confirmation also updates our earlier description of a compact circular digital console.

Earlier buyer communications suggest Honda BigWing in Lajpat Nagar, New Delhi, reportedly received two Rebel 300 motorcycles on November 4, both said to be E-Clutch versions. Deliveries are likely to start in coming days. These remain dealer-level estimates rather than a confirmed nationwide schedule.

raw_title: Hero’s Vida Delivers 600+ VX2 Scooters In A Single Day, Sets New Record
title: Hero's Vida Delivers 600+ VX2 Scooters In A Single Day, Sets New Record
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The Dhanteras delivery event earns an Asia Book of Records title, as Vida reports an 80 per cent YoY increase in October retail registrations Hero MotoCorp’s electric mobility brand Vida has secured an Asia Book of Records title after delivering more than 600 VX2 electric scooters in Jaipur on Dhanteras. The customer handovers took place at a single Vida centre in one day earning recognition for the highest number of electric scooters delivered in a day in a single city. The record comes at a time when the manufacturer has recorded a substantial increase in electric two-wheeler sales. The sales figures last month provide further context for the Jaipur achievement. Vida recorded an 80 per cent year-on-year increase in VAHAN retail registrations while its electric two-wheeler market share rose to 13.6 per cent from 11.1 per cent in October 2025. The difference amounts to 2.5 percentage points. Hero MotoCorp also reported 30,143 Vida scooter dispatches for October – a separate figure from customer retail registrations. The VX2 is available in five configurations: Go 2.2 kWh, Go 3.1 FB, Go 3.4 kWh, Plus 3.4 kWh, and Plus 4.4 kWh. The IDC-certified riding range varies between 92 km and 187 km based on battery capacity. The Go 3.1 FB offers a fixed battery and direct plug-in charging while removable battery arrangements are available on other versions. The different configurations appeal to those who have access to home charging as well as those who require removable batteries. The VX2 uses an electric motor capable of producing around 8 hp and 26 Nm of torque. The Plus 4.4 kWh variant has a claimed maximum speed of 90 kmph while the Plus 3.4 kWh reaches 80 kmph. The Go 2.2 kWh has a lower maximum speed of 70 kmph. Eco and Ride modes are offered on the Go variants and the Plus versions also receive a Sports mode for quicker throttle response. The Plus versions have a 4.3-inch TFT instrument display while the Go models use a 4.3-inch LCD screen. Smartphone connectivity, turn-by-turn navigation and over-the-air updates are available as part of the VX2’s features. The scooters also use a Combined Braking System and the Go 2.2 kWh offers up to 33.2 litres of storage beneath the seat. Vida has also established a charging and maintenance network for its electric scooters. The manufacturer reports more than 6,000 fast charging stations and over 700 service touchpoints in India. The infrastructure provides public charging access and authorised maintenance facilities for owners.

title: Honda's New SUV Brings Fresh Styling And Next-Gen Hybrid Tech
raw_summary: A new generation of the Avancier was teased by Honda Australia ahead of a local market launch. Honda has shared the first teaser of the next generation Avancier, ahead of its market launch in Australia. The new SUV is expected to boast a three-row layout and will introduce a sharper styling language. Furthermore, it will come fitted with the next-gen Honda Hybrid powertrain which is set to gradually replace the current e:HEV setup across the entire lineup.
summary: A new generation of the Avancier was teased by Honda Australia ahead of a local market launch. Honda has shared the first teaser of the next generation Avancier, ahead of its market launch in Australia. The new SUV is expected to boast a three-row layout and will introduce a sharper styling language.
article_paragraphs: A new generation of the Avancier was teased by Honda Australia ahead of a local market launch.

Honda has shared the first teaser of the next generation Avancier, ahead of its market launch in Australia. The new SUV is expected to boast a three-row layout and will introduce a sharper styling language. Furthermore, it will come fitted with the next-gen Honda Hybrid powertrain which is set to gradually replace the current e:HEV setup across the entire lineup.

The original Avancier was an Accord-based wagon sold in the Japanese market between 1999 and 2003. The second generation that followed in 2016 was a Chinese-built crossover from the GAC Honda joint venture, sharing its underpinnings with the previous-gen Acura MDX. Now, the same nameplate will be used for a new SUV, positioned above the CR-V.

The official teaser reveals the horizontal and vertical LEDs on the tailgate, flanking the simplified Honda emblem above the Avancier lettering. We can also see the sharp lines of the greenhouse, the integrated roof spoiler, and the slim headlights. The latter have a fancy starting sequence but their shape is reminiscent of the Range Rover Evoque, especially in combination with the contours of the hood.

The new design language is expected to be applied to future Hondas, such as the next iterations of the Civic and the Accord. As for the interior, the Avancier will likely offer a three-row seven-seater layout, with more space and practicality compared to the smaller CR-V .

More important than the exterior design of the Avancier is what lies under the skin. While the automaker didn't share any details about the specifications, the teaser video features Honda Hybrid lettering instead of the traditional e:HEV that has been used in electrified Hondas since 2020.

The new moniker suggests that the Avancier could be one of the very first models to adopt the next generation of Honda's self-charging hybrid setup , arriving in 2027. This promises to improve fuel economy by over 10%, while being 30% cheaper to produce compared to the previous system. The electrified powertrain is expected to be based around an updated 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine, likely inheriting the Honda S+Shift system from the Prelude coupe.

Production of the third-gen Honda Avancier will reportedly take place in Thailand. Besides Australia, it has been rumored that the SUV will also be offered in the Japanese market. Rivals will include the Hyundai Santa Fe, the Kia Sorento, the Toyota Kruger (Highlander), the Mazda CX-80, the VW Tayron, and the BYD Sealion 8.

title: New Hyundai Bayon Review
raw_summary: Hyundai Motor India has expanded its SUV lineup with the new Bayon, positioned between the Venue and Creta. It combines distinctive styling, a spacious cabin and a substantial technology package with Hyundai’s familiar 1.5-litre petrol engine. We drove the top-spec IVT variant in Goa to find out how this package comes together on the road. Prices for Hyundai Bayon start from Rs 9.99 lakh and it undercuts almost all of its immediate rivals. What Hyundai Bayon is, is a weapon forged in Hyundai crucible with its crosshairs on the chunk of the market occupied by Maruti Victoris. We drove the Bayon at the media drive in Goa and compiled our thoughts to tell you all about it.

article_paragraphs: Hyundai Motor India has expanded its SUV lineup with the new Bayon, positioned between the Venue and Creta. It combines distinctive styling, a spacious cabin and a substantial technology package with Hyundai’s familiar 1.5-litre petrol engine. We drove the top-spec IVT variant in Goa to find out how this package comes together on the road.

Prices for Hyundai Bayon start from Rs 9.99 lakh and it undercuts almost all of its immediate rivals. What Hyundai Bayon is, is a weapon forged in Hyundai crucible with its crosshairs on the chunk of the market occupied by Maruti Victoris. We drove the Bayon at the media drive in Goa and compiled our thoughts to tell you all about it.

Bayon is the latest iteration of Hyundai’s ‘Art Of Steel’ design language. It follows an Urban theme, made for younger audiences looking for a confident SUV stance to arrive in style. Bayon stands out, rather than blending in. The signature H-Edge LED DRLs along with high-intensity dual LED projector headlights look stunning.

The bold and sharp character lines, sculpted bonnet, flared wheel arches, wide rear haunches, machined 17-inch alloy wheels all lend a youthful and modern SUV appeal. At the rear, we can see a flared spoiler with Aero-style vertical high-mount stop lamp. There are no connected tail lights, for a change, which is a good thing.

There are six monotone colours, two dual tone colours and then two Matte colours with Bayon. The colour choice is important because they dictate the interior colour theme. If you go for dual-tone colours, they get an all-Black interior theme with Red contrasts for a sporty look, while other colours get a lighter Black and Olive Grey colour theme.

Speaking of interior, Hyundai Bayon gets a premium Digital Cabin dominated by the ‘Command Centre’ consisting of two 12.3-inch displays housed in a curved panoramic housing. The front seats get premium leatherette upholstery and then Hyundai has given soft-touch elements on door trims and then a fabric insert on dashboard to uplift overall cabin ambience.

There’s smart storage on dashboard and this is where we can see the ambient lighting, which also extends to door trims. The D-cut steering wheel gets Hyundai’s new quad dot branding and the steering wheel also houses the Drive Mode selector. Panoramic sunroof lets in a lot of light into the cabin making it feel luxurious and even rear quarter glass is appreciated too.

This tech-laded cabin is stuffed with features, creature comforts and modern amenities. For starters, there is wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, built-in navigation, Bose premium audio with subwoofer, powered driver’s seat, ventilated front seats, electronic parking brake, 360 cameras, blindspot alerts, blindspot monitoring, software-defined architecture with OTA updates on 19 controllers, auto-dimming IRVM, rear AC vents, wireless charger, auto AC and more.

title: Triumph Tracker 400 To Get TFT Screen, Cruise Control From Bonnie T40
raw_summary: Bajaj Auto is known to come up with an upgrade package and then this upgrade package trickles down to all of the, if not, most of their lineup. We saw this when the LCD instrument cluster was first introduced and more recently, we saw a new upgrade package with TFT cluster with Google Maps, ETB, Ride Modes, bi-directional quickshifter and traction control, among others. Now, a similar upgrade package seems to have been devised for Triumph Motorcycles by Bajaj and it made its debut with Bonneville T40. Recently we saw this upgrade package make its way to Thruxton 400 and now, we can see a similar upgrade package with Tracker 400 too and the test mule was spied recently, as seen in Vishal Patil’s video.

Recently we saw this upgrade package make its way to Thruxton 400 and now, we can see a similar upgrade package with Tracker 400 too and the test mule was spied recently, as seen in Vishal Patil’s video.

Bajaj and Triumph duo has not yet confirmed whether these upgrades spied with Thruxton 400 and now Tracker 400 will be launched as a new variant, or as standard equipment. Also, Bajaj and Triumph duo have not confirmed whether this upgrade package will make it to other Triumph 400 models like Speed 400, Scrambler 400X, Speed T4 and Scrambler 400XC.

Speaking of the upgrade package, it first debuted with the Bonneville T40 and is seen for the first time with Triumph’s TR Series of 400cc class motorcycles. This includes a 4-inch circular TFT instrument cluster that supports smartphone connectivity with music and call controls and then Google Maps mirroring.

With electronic throttle body, Triumph has introduced ride by wire, cruise control, traction control and then Ride Modes – Road, Rain, Eco, Rider A and Rider B. There’s lean-sensitive cornering ABS, lean-sensitive cornering traction control, self-canceling turn indicators, emergency deceleration warning and more.

The recent spy video by Vishal Patil does not confirm whether the Triumph Tracker 400 test mule gets all of these features from Bonneville T40 or only some of them. What we can see, is the presence of the new 4-inch circular TFT cluster along with the presence of the new switchgear, both shared with Bonneville T40.

The same 349cc single-cylinder liquid-cooled 4V engine as other Triumph TR Series motorcycles in India that is capable of generating 40 bhp of peak power and 32 Nm of peak torque, mated to a slipper clutch and a 6-speed gearbox. Launch is likely to happen soon.

raw_title: Mahindra XUV 3XO ZNG Scores 5 Stars In Bharat NCAP Crash Tests
title: Mahindra XUV 3XO ZNG Scores 5 Stars In Bharat NCAP Crash Tests
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Mahindra XUV 3XO ZNG has secured 29.36 points for adult protection and 45 points for child protection in the latest round of Bharat NCAP crash tests Mahindra introduced the XUV 3XO ZNG in October 2026 as a factory-fitted CNG alternative to its ICE compact SUV. Barely three weeks after its market introduction, the model has secured a five-star Bharat NCAP safety rating. The manufacturer claims that the ZNG is the first sub-compact CNG SUV in India to achieve the result. The new assessment comes two years after the regular XUV 3XO received its full marks from the same crash test organisation. The XUV 3XO ZNG uses a 1.2-litre, three-cylinder mStallion turbocharged engine that develops around 110 hp and 200 Nm of torque. Interestingly, the output is identical in petrol and CNG modes and maximum torque is available between 1,500rpm and 3,500rpm. A six-speed manual gearbox handles transmission duties. Mahindra claims acceleration from 0 to 60 kmph in 4.9 seconds and from 0 to 100 kmph in 11.8 seconds in CNG mode. Its certified fuel efficiency stands at 24.7km/kg. The dual-cylinder CNG system sits beneath the luggage compartment preserving a flat loading floor and 270 litres of boot capacity. The regular petrol XUV 3XO offers 364 litres and thus the CNG installation reduces usable luggage space by 94 litres. The spare wheel is mounted underneath the vehicle. The ZNG is sold in four variants – starting at Rs. 9.99 lakh for the MX Edge and going up to Rs. 12.27 lakh (both, ex-showroom) for the RevX A. Variant Price (ex-showroom) XUV 3XO ZNG MX Edge Rs. 9.99 lakh XUV 3XO ZNG RevX Edge (O) Rs. 10.79 lakh XUV 3XO ZNG AX5 Rs. 11.19 lakh XUV 3XO ZNG RevX A Rs. 12.27 lakh The Bharat NCAP assessment awarded the CNG SUV 29.36 points out of 32 for adult occupant protection and 45 out of 49 for child occupant protection. The adult score is identical to the regular XUV 3XO tested in 2024. However, the earlier model recorded 43 points for child protection – two points fewer than the newly announced ZNG result. The XUV 3XO ZNG has more than 35 standard safety features comprising six airbags, Electronic Stability Control, ISOFIX child-seat mounts and three-point seat belts for all passengers. The factory CNG installation also has an integrated gas-leak detection system. If a leak is detected, the system automatically switches the engine to petrol operation. A separate automatic switchover function operates when the CNG supply runs low. These protective measures are available from the base variant. The MX Edge gets a 10.25-inch infotainment touchscreen, cruise control, a reversing camera, rear air-conditioning vents and a 60:40 split rear seat. The AX5 receives twin 10.25-inch displays, dual-zone automatic climate control, alloy wheels and in-car connected functions. The top-spec RevX A features a sunroof, Dolby Atmos audio, black leatherette upholstery, and additional dark exterior detailing. The Tata Nexon CNG and Maruti Suzuki Brezza CNG are the key rivals to the Mahindra XUV 3XO ZNG. Its bookings and customer deliveries began last month.

raw_title: Royal Enfield Flying Flea Reaches Chennai, 14 Outlets Planned
title: Royal Enfield Flying Flea Reaches Chennai, 14 Outlets Planned
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The electric motorcycle brand will establish 14 sales and service touchpoints in Chennai taking its planned Indian retail network to 40 locations in four cities Royal Enfield has extended the availability of its Flying Flea C6 electric motorcycle to Chennai where 14 new sales and service touchpoints are planned. The city becomes the fourth Indian market for Flying Flea following Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Pune. The Chennai network will have two company operated stores and 12 partner outlets providing customers more locations to inspect the motorcycle, arrange test rides and access after-sales assistance. The dedicated Flying Flea stores will operate at OMR and Adyar while the remaining outlets will function alongside existing Royal Enfield dealerships. The locations are situated in areas such as Anna Nagar, Tambaram, Pallikaranai, Avadi, Tondiarpet and Nandanam. Royal Enfield has also identified 11 service centres in Chennai for routine maintenance and technical assistance. These centres will support the C6 as retail operations commence in the city. The brand already has 12 sales and service locations in Bengaluru, four in Hyderabad, and 10 in Pune. Chennai’s 14 new touchpoints will increase the planned network to 40 locations nationwide. Pune received its 10-centre network in late October, shortly before the Chennai announcement. The combination of dedicated showrooms and established Royal Enfield dealerships provides Flying Flea a retail presence in different parts of each city. The Flying Flea C6 costs Rs. 2.79 lakh while the Battery-as-a-Service option reduces the initial motorcycle price to Rs. 1.99 lakh (both prices, ex-showroom). The latter arrangement separates the battery cost from the initial vehicle purchase and requires a subscription payment. The upfront difference stands at Rs. 80,000 but the subscription charges must also be considered when comparing ownership costs. The motorcycle is available in Storm Black, Flea Green, and Parachute White. The C6 has a distinctive design inspired by the lightweight Royal Enfield Flying Flea motorcycles of the 1940s. A circular LED headlamp, slim upper bodywork, exposed forged-aluminium frame, and aluminium girder front fork distinguish it from other electric motorcycles. The compact battery assembly sits inside a magnesium enclosure beneath the tank-like upper section. The narrow rear bodywork, exposed structural components and lightweight styling also separate the C6 visually from the traditional Royal Enfield motorcycles. The electric motorcycle uses a 3.91 kWh battery and a permanent-magnet synchronous motor producing around 20.7 hp and 60 Nm of torque. Royal Enfield claims a maximum speed of 115 kmph and a riding range of 154 km under the Indian Driving Cycle. The electronics comprise five riding modes, traction control and lean-sensitive ABS. The C6 also has connected functions, smartphone integration and configurable electronic responses. Flying Flea is preparing a second electric motorcycle, the S6 scrambler, for a summer 2027 launch. Revealed at EICMA 2026, the S6 uses wire-spoke wheels, block-pattern tyres, an enduro-style seat, and a dedicated off-road riding mode. The scrambler shares its underlying architecture with the road-biased C6 but has different equipment for recreational trail riding.

raw_title: How Can Europe Accelerate Electric Trucking?
title: How Can Europe Accelerate Electric Trucking?
raw_summary: Europe is having a hard time lately, with skyrocketing oil prices dampening economies. Fuel costs, particularly diesel, are prompting surging interest in truck electrification. Europe has been urging truck makers to move toward electric trucking, and they have responded with a variety of electric semi trucks from many manufacturers. Europe is a group of sovereign countries with many standards. The European Union is a political and economic union of 27 states in that area. It issued directives urging action and imposing penalties. In response to European Union directives, companies have formed EV100, a coalition of corporations responding to the need. In a recent story, Steve Hanley wrote about European electric truck makers’ difficulties expanding truck electrification . Here’s a quotation from the story: “ In a letter to EU Commission president Ursula von der Leyen, of primary concern, in their estimation, is expanding the charging infrastructure for heavy-duty trucks in Europe.” There is no shortage of electric trucks in Europe. Expansion could go faster were it not for charging infrastructure. Manufacturers complain about “an alarming delay” in conditions needed to drive market uptake. For Europe, truck electrification is not working as well as in China, where over 90% of the world’s electric trucks reside. The differences between China and the EU show some reasons why truck electrification is slower in Europe. How did China succeed where the EU failed? China made electric trucks a freight system, not a vehicle category . Power is a major factor in electric grid infrastructure. Charging electric trucks places demands on power. Peak power determines how much infrastructure is necessary. In grid planning, peak annual power determines how much capital equipment is necessary. Reducing peak power demand is a critical factor for electric truck infrastructure. Figure 1 shows one method of reducing power called route stuffing. It schedules departures on heavy traffic corridors at regularly spaced intervals. Corridors like ones between ports and warehouses are a target for those practices. These corridors often route trucks in a round trip chain. Filling routes with scheduled trips can reduce power demand compared to random trip scheduling. The article Battery Swap Uses Fewer Batteries Than You Think is devoted to methods of analysis and planning that can lead to lower peak power demand. There are other benefits to planning, such as greater truck load capacity from the same amount of batteries. Part of the solution to slow electric truck infrastructure development is to plan infrastructure and truck use practices to reduce the charging power burden. Given the pressing and enduring need due to the diesel fuel cost crisis, it is necessary to reprioritize grid power upgrade demands. Demands for data center power upgrades like transformers for substations should be re shuffled and prioritized toward the diesel crisis.

Europe has been urging truck makers to move toward electric trucking, and they have responded with a variety of electric semi trucks from many manufacturers.
article_paragraphs: Europe is having a hard time lately, with skyrocketing oil prices dampening economies. Fuel costs, particularly diesel, are prompting surging interest in truck electrification. Europe has been urging truck makers to move toward electric trucking, and they have responded with a variety of electric semi trucks from many manufacturers. Europe is a group of sovereign countries with many standards. The European Union is a political and economic union of 27 states in that area. It issued directives urging action and imposing penalties. In response to European Union directives, companies have formed EV100, a coalition of corporations responding to the need. In a recent story, Steve Hanley wrote about European electric truck makers’ difficulties expanding truck electrification . Here’s a quotation from the story: “ In a letter to EU Commission president Ursula von der Leyen, of primary concern, in their estimation, is expanding the charging infrastructure for heavy-duty trucks in Europe.” There is no shortage of electric trucks in Europe. Expansion could go faster were it not for charging infrastructure. Manufacturers complain about “an alarming delay” in conditions needed to drive market uptake. For Europe, truck electrification is not working as well as in China, where over 90% of the world’s electric trucks reside. The differences between China and the EU show some reasons why truck electrification is slower in Europe. How did China succeed where the EU failed? China made electric trucks a freight system, not a vehicle category .

Power is a major factor in electric grid infrastructure. Charging electric trucks places demands on power. Peak power determines how much infrastructure is necessary. In grid planning, peak annual power determines how much capital equipment is necessary. Reducing peak power demand is a critical factor for electric truck infrastructure. Figure 1 shows one method of reducing power called route stuffing. It schedules departures on heavy traffic corridors at regularly spaced intervals. Corridors like ones between ports and warehouses are a target for those practices. These corridors often route trucks in a round trip chain. Filling routes with scheduled trips can reduce power demand compared to random trip scheduling. The article Battery Swap Uses Fewer Batteries Than You Think is devoted to methods of analysis and planning that can lead to lower peak power demand. There are other benefits to planning, such as greater truck load capacity from the same amount of batteries. Part of the solution to slow electric truck infrastructure development is to plan infrastructure and truck use practices to reduce the charging power burden. Given the pressing and enduring need due to the diesel fuel cost crisis, it is necessary to reprioritize grid power upgrade demands. Demands for data center power upgrades like transformers for substations should be re shuffled and prioritized toward the diesel crisis.

In two articles, Michael Barnard outlined the issues. Vehicles are not a transportation system. What does Europe have now? It has an EU Commission interacting with a coalition, EV100. The problem is, there are plenty of trucks available, but who is in charge of infrastructure? You can’t have electric trucks without means of charging, but as the coalition complains, “Significant improvements to charging infrastructure, a reduction in carbon dioxide based tolls, and a coherent policy framework are urgently needed.” There are so many stakeholders — including the commission, vehicles makers, and charging companies across multiple countries — that no one is in charge of infrastructure, and without it, nothing moves. It needs a unity of purpose and action.

If China is succeeding, why not adopt its strategy? Perhaps the answer is right in front of everyone’s nose. As Michael puts it, “the policy connects vehicles to corridors, depots, service areas, grids and freight use cases instead of treating sales targets as sufficient.” CATL offered Europe a system, not a vehicle. This is a “turn key” solution. It’s a well thought out system, including use of methods and practices, not an anything goes free-for-all. That kind of stability and predictability is what EV100 leaders are looking for. This is not a swap-or-nothing scenario. Different techniques apply to various use cases. Swap must be planned for high-use freight corridors and other proper applications. Swap trucks can also fast charge or slow charge, providing flexibility and a system of trucks that includes smaller trucks, not just semis.

What does all this have to do with Europe’s slowly advancing infrastructure? Simply put, electric trucks put heavy charging demands on the grid. Trucks can have megawatt-hour batteries that require megawatt power charging to charge in an hour. Reducing grid power demands can reduce grid infrastructure upgrade costs, and leverage capital investment toward faster implementation.

“The process of getting megawatt charging equipment connected to the grid can take several years, delaying deployment even where operators and infrastructure providers are ready to invest.” The need for megawatt charging equipment is reduced by accelerating swap network development instead of fixed battery trucks that must be charged by fast chargers. “ Swaptopus is easy to misread as a quirky name for another electric-truck infrastructure project. It is a newly formed joint venture between Octopus Energy and CATL, created to develop automated battery-swapping hubs for heavy trucks across Europe.” Unlike the government of China that played a role in encouraging standards and cooperation in infrastructure, Europe has a looser arrangement between many countries with various standards. Europe is learning the slow, hard way where battery swapping is most needed .

Every truck application has different optimization. It means that there must be different approaches to fit freight operations in heavy traffic corridors. Quoting Michael Barnard, “Freight operators often run repeated routes between ports, factories, distribution centres and logistics hubs. Those patterns provide known traffic, known stopping points and relatively predictable electricity demand. A swap hub can be placed around an existing freight flow instead of hoping that enough unrelated trucks eventually pass through.”

Freight corridors are a scenario made to order for battery swap. Real trucking solutions include a mix of vehicle and infrastructure types — from small, local delivery, to large, long-haul freight; and from slow, overnight charging, to medium power charging and battery swap — all used in concert to accelerate heavy truck electrification. With a wide variety of charging options, and vehicles and charging use cases targeted in coordination to avoid peak power demands, the path forward is eased. School buses don’t need expensive high-power fast charging. Lower-power chargers can do the trick. Local delivery can use a mix of overnight and medium power charging. Heavy truck dispatch must be more carefully coordinated to avoid peak demand and grid upgrade costs. A mix of medium-power charging and swap stations along with planned use cases can successfully lower electric freight power needs and transport system capital expenses to speed transport electrification.

title: Thermal Dawn
raw_summary: Another great idea from Down Under: Thermal Dawn promises cost effective heating and cooling, mainly by replacing gas boilers in cold climates. CleanTechnica had a chance to interview Nick Zeniou, Founder of Thermal Dawn, recently by phone, fresh after his presentation at Everything Electric. You can hear him explain his revolutionary system here , or here with a little less drama. Everything Electric was a good opportunity to measure public reaction to the new product. Nick tells me that hundreds of people checked out their stall. “People care about carbon cost and comfort. People don’t compromise on comfort.” Sounds like comfort trumps carbon cost. Homeowners who visited the stand and filled out the survey were focused on sustainability and cost. article_paragraphs: Another great idea from Down Under: Thermal Dawn promises cost effective heating and cooling, mainly by replacing gas boilers in cold climates. CleanTechnica had a chance to interview Nick Zeniou, Founder of Thermal Dawn, recently by phone, fresh after his presentation at Everything Electric. You can hear him explain his revolutionary system here , or here with a little less drama.

Everything Electric was a good opportunity to measure public reaction to the new product. Nick tells me that hundreds of people checked out their stall. “People care about carbon cost and comfort. People don’t compromise on comfort.” Sounds like comfort trumps carbon cost. Homeowners who visited the stand and filled out the survey were focused on sustainability and cost. Nick cautions: “it was an electrification expo crowd, and 50 of the 62 already had solar, so it’s not the whole market.” See the chart below.

Although I live in the warmer part of Australia (Brisbane), many Aussies have to endure cold winters. Nick tells me he is looking at installs in Sydney, Canberra, and Melbourne in the deep south. Thermal Dawn can store heat up to 70 degrees Celsius, or down to 5 degrees. Thermal Dawns’ equipment can run cold or hot water through pipes and radiators that are already installed, depending on the need — without having to run an expensive gas boiler. He describes it as a thermal battery. Just to be clear, it does not generate electricity.

Check out this graph below, which shows the Thermal Dawn system in action at a house in Melbourne during a day in August 2026. It shows room temperature and when the heat pump was running, in 15-minute samples, unedited. The heat pump ran until about 1:45pm, then not again, heated by stored energy through the evening peak.

“What about return on investment,” I asked. He described two systems they have had running over the southern Australian winter which have saved the homeowners approximately AU$1,500 each. “The first was a house in Melbourne, our first install, live since May 2026. The owners charge the system in their retailer’s free three-hour midday window, so the heat for the evening costs them close to nothing. The second was a Warragul (slab-heated home, Victoria): installed in two days in July 2026. Our controls turn the home’s concrete slab into part of the battery, managing when it charges and when it releases heat. On 95% of winter evenings, the heat pumps did not run at all between 5 pm and 9pm. Since commissioning, 70,521 MJ of gas has been avoided by just these two installations.”

Nick further explains: “A standard heat pump draws from the grid during those expensive morning and evening hours. You’ve escaped gas, but you’re still paying premium rates every time the temperature drops at night. Thermal Dawn is different. Our system charges when power is cheapest, a free midday window, your own solar, or late-night off-peak, then delivers that stored warmth through your radiators and underfloor heating all evening, with the compressor off through the expensive hours.

It appears that Thermal Dawn’s secret sauce is “Phase Change Materials.” Naturally, Nick declined to share exactly what Thermal Dawn is using. The system replaces a gas boiler with a combination of reverse cycle heat pump, well insulated water tank, and phase change materials. PCMs are designed to freeze or melt at a specific temperature, storing and releasing heat when they change physical state, usually from solid to liquid. “PCM doubles our heat capacity.” The heating applications I could understand, what about the cooling? “Cool water from the tank runs through a fan coil unit, and the fan blows cool air into the room. Cooling is an optional add-on.” That’s the answer.

How do thermal storage and a home battery/solar system work together? “Thermal storage is cheap storage doing one job very well. Heating, cooling, and hot water are the largest, most predictable loads in the house, and covering them thermally is far cheaper per kWh than covering them from lithium. A battery is expensive storage doing a general-purpose job.

title: XPENG Researchers and Academic Partners Introduce GroundingPI, An Open-Source Visual Perception Model For Physical AI
raw_summary: Guangzhou, China — XPENG (NYSE: XPEV, HKEX: 9868), a leading Physical AI company, has supported the development of GroundingPI, an open-source visual perception foundation model created by researchers affiliated with XPENG, Peking University, The University of Hong Kong and other academic institutions. The research explores a new approach to embodied intelligence by focusing on a fundamental capability: enabling AI systems to accurately identify objects and understand their spatial positions in the physical world. With approximately 4 billion parameters, GroundingPI achieved the highest aggregate score among 44 baseline models evaluated across 34 perception benchmarks covering 11 capability categories.

article_paragraphs: Guangzhou, China — XPENG (NYSE: XPEV, HKEX: 9868), a leading Physical AI company, has supported the development of GroundingPI, an open-source visual perception foundation model created by researchers affiliated with XPENG, Peking University, The University of Hong Kong and other academic institutions.

The research explores a new approach to embodied intelligence by focusing on a fundamental capability: enabling AI systems to accurately identify objects and understand their spatial positions in the physical world. With approximately 4 billion parameters, GroundingPI achieved the highest aggregate score among 44 baseline models evaluated across 34 perception benchmarks covering 11 capability categories.
The research paper, model weights and supporting code have been made publicly available, enabling researchers and developers to further explore perception-focused approaches to Physical AI.
As AI increasingly moves beyond digital environments into physical applications such as robotics and autonomous driving, accurately understanding the surrounding environment becomes essential.

While general-purpose foundation models have demonstrated strong capabilities in language understanding, reasoning and planning, physical intelligence requires more precise visual perception. AI systems must not only recognize objects but also identify their exact locations and spatial relationships to support real-world interaction.

GroundingPI takes a perception-focused approach to this challenge. Rather than relying on robot action labels during the perceptual model’s training, the research focuses on developing foundational visual understanding capabilities that can support downstream action-learning systems.

For example, when instructed to identify “the handle of the cup on the right”, an AI system needs to locate not only the correct cup but also the precise position of its handle. GroundingPI is designed to represent such information using spatial coordinates, including points and bounding boxes.

The model is trained across 11 categories of perceptual capabilities, including object detection, dense object localization, referring expression grounding, optical character recognition (OCR), document layout understanding, user interface element recognition and robotic spatial localization.

The production-spec model showcased uses a dual-tone white and black colour theme. More colour options are expected when the scooter is launched.

Wheels are orange coloured, which add contrast and ensure a more dynamic presence. Black-finished surfaces utilize a mix of matte black and glossy black. Distinctive graphics have been used in black and orange shades. The scooter uses a single piece seat with a stepped design. The model showcased can be seen with a rack and top box. These are likely to be offered as accessories.

TVS M1-S has relatively modest specifications and does not appear to be part of the race for higher range and top speed. The focus could be more on accessibility, practical applications, reliability, durability and easy maintenance. The scooter is equipped with a 4.2 kWh lithium-ion NMC battery pack, offering a range of around 120 km (European WMTC testing standards).

The battery is installed in the floorboard, ensuring a low centre of gravity and optimized weight distribution. TVS M1-S uses a permanent magnet synchronous electric motor, bolted on the chassis. It generates 12.5 kW or approximately 17 PS. Continuous output is rated at 5 kW or 6.80 PS. The scooter has a top speed of 105 km/h.

TVS M1-S has a 1.8 kW onboard charger. It can achieve 10% to 80% charge in around 1 hour 15 minutes. Core hardware parts include telescopic front forks and twin rear shock absorbers. Both ends have 14-inch wheels, paired with 110/70 front and 120/70 rear tyres. 230 mm discs have been used on both wheels and dual-channel ABS is being offered as standard.

With a seat height of 800 mm, TVS M1-S is suited for agile handling across urban environments. It also gets a high ground clearance of 170 mm. The scooter has a kerb weight of 150 kg and comes with 26 litres of underseat storage. At the front, there’s a glovebox and an open compartment for small items.

M1-S is equipped with premium features such as cruise control and a tyre pressure monitoring system. A USB Type-A charging port has been provided at the front. The scooter also gets advanced functions like app-based seat unlocking, key-fob ignition and ‘Find my Bike’. A 7-inch TFT instrument cluster has been used with support for Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and onboard LTE connectivity.

Boles Manufacturing was founded in Burbank, California, in 1946 – the company built a popular line of aluminum travel trailers for 34 years, and it had all started out with a single trailer built in a one-car garage. The Boles Aero never reached Airstream’s national popularity , but their polished aluminum trailers developed a cult following all their own.

Boles Manufacturing was founded in Burbank, California, in 1946 – the company built a popular line of aluminum travel trailers for 34 years, and it had all started out with a single trailer built in a one-car garage. Image courtesy of Boles Aero.
The company was founded by Don and Jeanette Boles, and their built their trailers using methods Don had learned making aircraft.

In 1939, Don Boles was one of the first 37 candidates picked for a new four-year tool and die apprenticeship. The US Department of Labor had set it up as part of the Roosevelt administration’s plan to pull the country out of the Great Depression. It was an interesting time in world history, WWII kicked off that same year across the Atlantic, and two years later the United States would join the conflict after the attack on Pearl Harbor.

Boles served it at Lockheed’s aircraft plant in Burbank, learning aircraft design and construction methods, and he went on to win several awards for tools he designed to improve the way aluminum parts were made. He graduated as a journeyman tool and die maker in 1943, right in the midst of WWII when men with his skillset were in huge demand.

After a short assignment with General Electric in Cleveland, Ohio, Boles enlisted in the U.S. Navy and was posted to a base at Norman, Oklahoma. No housing could be found there for his wife, Jeanette, and their three children, so he bought a used 27 foot trailer, and the family lived in it for the rest of his military service. The couple had met at Burbank High School and married a month after she graduated, when she was 16 and he was 18.

Everyone knows that electric cars are much more inconvenient than gas cars. After all, there is a gas station on every corner and it only takes 5 minutes to fill up. Electric chargers are rare, and it takes at least an hour to charge.
Wrong: If you have access to 220 volt electricity or a L2 charger at home or work, an electric vehicle is much more convenient than a gas car for 300 miles per day of local driving.
In principal: In the evening, you drive into your garage, carport or driveway and take 10 seconds to plug in, the next morning, you have a full charge and take 10 seconds to unplug.

Compare that with a gas car. You probably have to make a couple of special trips per week to the gas station, put in your credit card, grab the smelly nozzle, put it in your car, and wait five minutes to fill. Then you return the smelly nozzle to the pump.
With the gas car, every 3,000 miles, you need to go to a Jiffy Lube and sit in their smelly waiting room for an hour while they change your oil.
With the gas car, every year, you need to go to an inspection station and wait an hour in their smelly waiting room while they do an emissions check.
These three tasks are all eliminated with an electric vehicle, which makes it much more convenient for local driving.

raw_summary: Your car is getting “long in tooth,” or maybe your daughter is going away to college and you are giving her your car. Whatever the reason, you are looking for another car. summary: Your car is getting “long in tooth,” or maybe your daughter is going away to college and you are giving her your car. Whatever the reason, you are looking for another car. It could be new, it could be used: don’t even look at gas cars, electric cars are superior technology!
article_paragraphs: Your car is getting “long in tooth,” or maybe your daughter is going away to college and you are giving her your car. Whatever the reason, you are looking for another car. It could be new, it could be used: don’t even look at gas cars, electric cars are superior technology!

The wheels on every railroad locomotive in the world are driven by electric motors. All the busiest rail routes in Europe and China are pure electric, including high-speed rail. 98% of new cars in Norway are electric, over 80% of new cars in Denmark are electric. In China, the country with the largest sales of new cars in the world, the percentage of new electric cars in September 2026 was 67%. 82% of the operating bus fleet in China is electric. Even ships and airplanes are going electric. The data is unequivocal: electric propulsion is superior to internal combustion propulsion. Only the huge political contributions to Trump by the fossil fuel industry and his resulting anti-EV policies have slowed down adoption in this country.

In places we’ve been like California; Portland, Oregon; and northern Utah, you are seeing a lot of Teslas, so you know that electric cars are working for a lot of people these days. It’s time for you to do some research on electric cars.

You do pay a premium for new electric cars, because the batteries are still quite expensive. If price is the driving factor for you, buy a used electric car. Hardly any used EVs are high mileage, and EV batteries still have plenty of life even after they go off warranty at 8 years and 120,000 miles. There are thousands of lightly used EVs sitting at used car lots at reasonable prices all over the country these days. Some used car dealers will give you an estimate of the battery life. If not, get a friend who is an experienced EV driver to help you evaluate the battery life of the EV you are considering.

If you just do local driving or have two cars and have a garage or off-street parking, an EV is a no brainer. EVs are hands-down more convenient than gas cars for local driving. Your EV will have plenty of range for local driving, it will get a complete charge overnight in your home garage refueling station and it will never need an oil change.

EVs are as quiet as mice, as smooth as kittens, and as quick as jackrabbits. They have simple electric motors, not complex internal combustion engines. They have simple one-speed transmissions, not complex 7-speed automatic transmissions. They don’t have exhaust systems with mufflers that will rust and need replacement. They don’t have emission control systems with limited life. They don’t have complex cooling systems with big radiators. You seldom use your brakes with an EV, so your brakes may last the life of the car. They don’t have a big lead-acid battery for starting, with a maximum life of 5 years. New EVs have only a small lithium-ion battery, which lasts 10+ years. Bottom line: Routine maintenance for EVs is almost nil. I think the only real maintenance item on a Tesla over the first 3 years is the cabin air filter. You can expect an EV to go 500,000 miles without major repair or replacement in most cases.

Perhaps you can stomach buying a car from Tesla whose CEO has become one of the most despicable persons on the planet lately. (Example: Musk recently suspended access to his Starlink communications system to the Ukrainians who are valiantly defending their country from the Russian aggressors.) However, Tesla has sold almost 10 million automobiles worldwide that don’t emit CO2 and particulate pollution while operating. Tesla also has by far the most ubiquitous charging system, which allows cross-country driving on major US roads with little planning. Consider buying a Tesla.

So, what about cross-country trips? Everyone knows that long-distance trips in an electric car are inconvenient or even impossible, because there aren’t enough charging stations and it takes an hour if you can find one. Wrong: Every 100 miles along all the major Interstate highways, Tesla has built Superchargers with 8 to 32 and a few with over 100 charging stalls. By the time you have gone to the bathroom, walked the dog, and chatted with a fellow EV owner for a few minutes, you probably have more than enough charge to continue your journey. Usually, charging takes about 20 minutes. If you need a longer charge, you may need to watch a bit of Octopus Teacher or Back to the Future II on the big screen in the car for another 10 minutes.

Whatever the reason, you are looking for another car.

This year’s summit is the first to be held in Korea . Chang Hwan Kim, Executive Vice President and Head of the Electrification Energy Solutions Tech Unit at Hyundai Motor Group, is the first Korean to serve as FISITA P resident .

“Hyundai Motor Group will continue to strengthen its competitiveness in key future mobility technologies and continue to participate in technology exchange and collaboration across the global automotive industry to contribute to the development of the future mobility sector.” –Chang Hwan Kim, Executive Vice President and Head of the Electrification Energy Solutions Tech Unit at Hyundai Motor Group

On the first day, Manfred Harrer, President and Head of R&D Division at Hyundai Motor Group, delivered a keynote address introducing the Group’s electrification strategy . It encompasses battery electric vehicles (BEVs), hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), extended-range electric vehicles (EREVs) and fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs). Harrer described the Group’s technology development roadmap for responding flexibly to market changes and customer needs.

Harrer also emphasized strengthening future vehicle development capabilities by combining engineering technology with AI-based digital capabilities and connecting the strengths of different technologies to pursue a sustainable mobility future.

In his opening remarks, Kim said that the automotive industry is undergoing an unprecedented technological transition. He emphasized that diverse technology approaches and stronger global collaboration are important to the advancement of future mobility.

Under the theme “Embracing the Complexities of Mobility,” the summit is addressing key technologies and challenges facing the automotive industry, including software-defined vehicles (SDVs), AI, autonomous driving, batteries and energy infrastructure .
